stories.Headline: SK Hynix Rises 2.4% After Altman’s Korea Visit on HBM Supply, AI Infrastructure Talks
stories.Summary:
SK Hynix shares rose 2.4% after OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman visited South Korea, according to a report by Walter Bloomberg on Nov. 2. During the visit, Altman met with SK Group executives to discuss HBM supply and issues related to building Stargate AI infrastructure. The talks drew attention to high-bandwidth memory supply and cooperation on artificial intelligence infrastructure. The share move followed the visit and the reports about the discussions.

SK Hynix said customer requests for HBM supply are currently more than double the volume it can provide. Nomura maintained a positive outlook on SK Hynix, and Rosenblatt reaffirmed its buy rating while dismissing recent concerns about intensifying competition. A separate report said SK Hynix may issue a special dividend of about $12 billion related to gains from its investment in Kioxia. A decision on the special dividend has not been finalized.

The articles do not name who at SK Group met Altman or give further details of what was agreed. They do not say what specific requirements or changes the talks would bring beyond the HBM supply and Stargate infrastructure discussions. No next steps are stated beyond the reported talks and the unresolved special dividend question. More to follow.

Articles.Title: SK Hynix Rises 2.4% After Altman’s Korea Visit on HBM Supply, AI Infrastructure Talks - bloomingbit

stories.Headline: Humanity at Crossroads With AI, Former Science Minister Warns
stories.Summary:
Kim Jin-hyun, a former South Korean minister of science and technology who is now in his 90s, sent Seoul Economic Daily a copy of his book "AI and the Remaking of the Nation," published last month, along with a handwritten letter calling it a dedication to his country and a will for later generations. He met a reporter from the newspaper at his office in Pangyo, Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, on the 2nd. In the interview he said humanity stands at a crossroads, whether it will coexist with AI or meet its end in a counterattack by its own creations. He urged leaders, starting with the president and members of the National Assembly, to defend liberal democracy and the market economy and to marshal national strength to remake the nation.

He said Korea should not chase slogans like becoming one of the top three AI powers, and should instead set national security and public safety as its goals first and then pick the AI technologies to achieve them. He named eight strategic technologies: future food and next-generation energy for survival, quantum, future-oriented defense, and cyber and cognitive warfare for security, and sovereign AI, space infrastructure and physical AI for growth. He called for transitional national policies to handle the unemployment and industrial restructuring expected on the way to the singularity era, which futurist Ray Kurzweil predicted would arrive in 2045, though some see it in the 2030s. He proposed a ministry of science, technology and self-reliance as a fourth branch of power, or as a second-best option second and third premierships for self-reliance, and at minimum an ombudsman to advise on science and technology policy.

He said Korea became the first testbed in the AI world because traditional, early modern and modern problems all erupted at once during compressed growth, and he cited historian Yuval Noah Harari describing Korea as the best laboratory for observing how new technologies affect human society. He said that by the standard of self-reliance, meaning self-sufficiency in food and energy for public safety and in national security, Korea is an unfinished nation. On energy he said small modular reactors are commercially viable and practical for a country as small as Korea, and that fusion power faces the obstacle of stabilizing plasma, which may become possible if quantum computers reach 200,000 qubits. He said sustained state research funding is needed, and that people of conscience and responsibility must steel themselves to build the new world AI has set in motion.

Articles.Title: Humanity at Crossroads With AI, Former Science Minister Warns - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Chief Says AI Industry Is Still at 'Jan. 1'
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electro-Mechanics held a ceremony marking its 53rd anniversary at its Suwon plant on Oct. 2, and CEO Chang Duck-hyun gave a commemorative address there. Executives and employees attended in person, while staff at domestic and overseas sites joined through the company's internal broadcast network. In his speech, Chang said the global artificial intelligence industry is still only at Jan. 1. He said AI servers and data centers are expanding, which is sharply raising demand for core components and the technical difficulty of making them.

Chang said the company's main businesses, including multilayer ceramic capacitors and semiconductor package substrates, have been handed an unprecedented large-scale growth opportunity. He pointed to global partnerships, an unrivaled product portfolio and proven production capacity as company strengths. He said what matters now is execution. He called for stronger execution across development, production, quality, and safety and environment so the growth opportunity turns into tangible results.

Chang also urged employees to change how they work by using AI. He said AI technology is fundamentally redefining the way humans work. He asked every employee to use their own specialized AI agent to streamline simple, repetitive tasks and focus on creative, high-value work. The ceremony also gave awards to long-serving employees and to top teams from an in-house AI hackathon. The company recently held the hackathon to strengthen employees' AI skills, and it selected projects with strong potential for on-site application, such as manufacturing process optimization and work automation.

Articles.Title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Chief Says AI Industry Is Still at 'Jan. 1' - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Bespin Global Launches AI Agent That Runs Office Tasks
stories.Summary:
Bespin Global, an artificial intelligence services company, said on November 3, 2026, that it had launched HelpNow Computer, an AI agent that automatically handles a range of office tasks. The work runs from entering data into internal systems to drafting documents and analyzing data. The agent goes beyond answering questions and operates a company's internal systems directly to carry out work. When a user requests a task in natural language, the AI draws up an execution plan and moves across multiple programs to complete the necessary steps in order.

The agent can log into a company's enterprise resource planning system or groupware to enter data and submit various applications and filings. It also drafts and edits documents in formats including PDF, Word, Excel and Hangul, and analyzes internal data to compile reports. Repetitive tasks can be saved as separate functions and reused. Because the AI operates internal systems directly, the company has built in security features, with all tasks running in a virtual environment isolated from outside networks. High-risk actions can be set to require employee approval, and the service also supports access restrictions by employee and logging of task histories.

The service is offered in subscription and on-premise versions, and it can be deployed on cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Naver Cloud, as well as on a company's internal servers and closed networks cut off from the external internet. Bespin Global plans to start by having the AI observe tasks and propose execution plans, then expand the scope of actual work it performs based on the results of that review. Park Ki-chul, head of Bespin Global's HelpNow development division, said that for AI to deliver real value in corporate settings, it has to move beyond understanding to execution. He added that HelpNow Computer is an enterprise AI agent that turns employees' work requests into actual results.

Articles.Title: Bespin Global Launches AI Agent That Runs Office Tasks - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea Plans AI Clusters but Sets Aside No Budget for Them
stories.Summary:
The South Korean government has decided to build artificial intelligence clusters that bring together AI companies, institutions and talent, but it included no money for the project in its 2027 budget proposal. The Ministry of Science and ICT had asked for about 4 billion won to support region-specific AI programs centered on the clusters, including running a dedicated agency. That request was not reflected during budget review by the Ministry of Planning and Budget, according to relevant ministries and the National Assembly on the 1st. An AI cluster is a designated zone that gathers companies and institutions doing AI research and development.

Under the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation of Trust, which took effect in January this year, central and local governments may give administrative, financial and technical support to AI clusters. The government plans to accept applications from local governments next year and establish national AI clusters across the country. It intends to form a review committee of government officials and private-sector experts, then designate clusters based on criteria such as whether skilled workers can be readily secured and whether a site can be linked to a region's main industries to help create jobs. Local governments can also set up AI clusters on their own under the act and its presidential decree, but a cluster designated as national is expected to receive central government support more easily.

An official at the Ministry of Science and ICT said the ministry is preparing procedures including a public notice for cluster designation, and that the scale and form of support for designated sites are still under discussion. A ministry official said the ministry will work to have the budget reflected during parliamentary review. An industry official said there is no particular reason for a company to relocate unless proper benefits are offered to tenants. A local government official said the absence of a central budget for building or operating the clusters appears to mean government support will not be available, and that a designated site will end up only half-complete if tenant companies and institutions cannot be properly supported.

Separately, the Ministry of Science and ICT has drawn up 9.4 trillion won in AI-related spending for next year, an increase of about 4.3 trillion won, or 84.3%, from this year. That accounts for 31.8% of the ministry's total budget proposal of about 29.6 trillion won. Of that amount, the government plans to channel 5.6 trillion won, or 59.6%, into securing top-tier AI models and technologies, including homegrown AI foundation models, next-generation AI technology and AI security. The government also allocated 1.9 trillion won for AI services and adoption and 1.2 trillion won for building an inclusive AI society.

Articles.Title: Korea Plans AI Clusters but Sets Aside No Budget for Them - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Google Legend Jeff Dean Bets on AI That Runs Its Own Experiments
stories.Summary:
Jeff Dean, who joined Google in 1999 as its 30th employee and left in August as chief scientist after 27 years, spoke on Oct. 28 at Stanford University in Palo Alto, California, at an AI event titled "Confronting Our AI Future: Hope, Fear, and the Choices Ahead." He was the final speaker at the event, which ran from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and included presentations and panel discussions. News of his departure became public on Aug. 5, the day Google's share price fell 4%.

He left Google at age 58, having been born in July 1968, and started a company. The company is Discovery Loop, founded by four former Google researchers: Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le and Dean. It is developing an automated model in which AI proposes research hypotheses, runs thousands of experiments at once and adjusts the hypotheses based on the results. The company is a public benefit corporation, and Dean said its mission is to build approaches that can automatically solve important problems in machine learning and engineering. He said the goal is to improve the productivity of domain experts by 20 to 50 times, not to replace people.

Dean said the team spent its first three months focused on building a strong founding team and hiring excellent people early. He said about 20 automatic improvement loops are currently running, and the company has built an agent harness, an execution environment that sets the standards by which AI carries out work. He said the harness can scale so that hundreds of thousands of agents can perform tasks. He described the technology as automating the experimental loop so that later experiments improve on earlier ones, and he said he believes it can have a remarkable positive impact on the world if used correctly.

Reports last month said Chen Guangyu, a 17-year-old scientist born in 2009 who worked on the Kimi K3 model at China's Moonshot AI, had joined Discovery Loop, though the accuracy of that report had not been established. Dean did not name him, but his presentation indirectly confirmed Chen's arrival. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, with 2.8 trillion parameters, in July, and Chen was a co-author of the Attention Residuals paper released by the Kimi team in March. Discovery Loop declined an interview request from Seoul Economic Daily, saying it was currently at the stage of focusing on building the organization.

Articles.Title: Google Legend Jeff Dean Bets on AI That Runs Its Own Experiments - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Korea Tourism Organization to Host AI Transformation Seminar
stories.Summary:
The Korea Tourism Organization said on Nov. 3 that it will hold the 2026 Tourism AX (AI Transformation) Seminar on Jan. 13 at COEX in Samseong-dong, Seoul, together with the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The event will be held under the theme "Tourism's Next Journey: Checking In With AI." Technology companies from Korea and abroad, lodging platforms and travel content specialists will take part to outline how AI adoption is reshaping the tourism industry. Oh Jung-sik, a director at Naver Cloud, and Lee Gun-bok, a vice president at Microsoft Korea, will give talks on AI technology trends at home and abroad and the future of the tourism industry.

A panel discussion will follow, in which experts and attendees will discuss the challenges facing the tourism industry as it adopts AI and the direction it should take. Tourism companies will also present their own AI use cases. Oh Hyun-seok, chief executive of ONDA, a business-to-business lodging reservation management platform, will present cases of AI-driven business innovation at tourism ventures. Travel YouTuber "Ttoddeonam," who has 700,000 subscribers, will deliver a special lecture on travelers and tourism marketing in the age of AI.

The event is open not only to tourism industry workers but to anyone interested in tourism. Applications will be accepted through the 11th on the Tourism e-Learning Center website. The seminar will also be streamed live online for those unable to attend in person. Min Byung-sun, head of the Tourism Industry Division at the Korea Tourism Organization, said the AI transformation is no longer a choice but an essential task for the survival and advancement of Korea's tourism industry. He said he hopes the seminar will serve as an opportunity to offer industry workers practical business solutions.

Articles.Title: Korea Tourism Organization to Host AI Transformation Seminar - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Hana Asset Management Sees Tighter AI Stock Picking in 2027
stories.Summary:
Hana Asset Management held a briefing in Yeouido, Seoul, on Nov. 2, 2026, marking its third anniversary, where Kim Jun-rae, head of its global multi-asset management division, set out the firm's outlook for 2027. The firm said AI investment will continue even in a high-rate environment, but returns will diverge based on companies' profitability and ability to raise funds. It said investors should keep semiconductors at the core of their portfolios while broadening exposure to software, cybersecurity and cloud services tied to AI monetization, and be more selective about individual names. Kim described 2027 global equities as a year of holding core growth stocks while choosing names and themes more carefully.

Kim said the screening criteria are return on invested capital, cash flow and upward revisions to earnings forecasts. With solid U.S. growth and fiscal pressures likely to keep rates high, he said investors need to check whether companies earn returns on invested capital that exceed their funding costs. He said portfolios should center on semiconductors, where Big Tech capital spending becomes revenue, while widening focus to software, cybersecurity and cloud. In software he pointed to companies shifting from per-user to usage-based pricing as AI agents spread, and in cloud he said large, high-quality providers with strong margins and credit profiles have the advantage. The fixed-income division said bonds are becoming more attractive, offering yields of around 4% a year with the prospect of price gains if rates fall, and the Hana 1Q ETF Solutions team presented AI, bonds and crypto as key ETF themes for next year.

Chief Executive Kim Tae-woo said that if the past three years were about laying the company's foundation and proving its potential, the next three years will be about achieving greater growth together with partners. He said the firm will become a true house of excellence in retirement pension asset management, where clients can entrust their assets with confidence for the long term. Hana Asset Management marked its third anniversary that day and has grown its ETF net assets about 13-fold to 4.5403 trillion won as of the end of September from 350 billion won when it launched in 2023. The number of ETF products rose to 27 from four, and net assets in target-date funds reached 484.6 billion won.

Articles.Title: Hana Asset Management Sees Tighter AI Stock Picking in 2027 - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Hanmi Pharmaceutical Shifts Health App Chatbot to Korean AI
stories.Summary:
Hanmi Pharmaceutical signed a four-way memorandum of understanding on Jan. 30 at its C&C Square in Seoul's Songpa District to move the chatbot on its digital health platform eppiday onto Korean-built AI. The partners are AI chip maker FuriosaAI, AI solutions provider Xperix and Bagel Labs, Xperix's health care subsidiary. Hanmi announced the agreement on the 2nd. The aim is to reduce reliance on overseas cloud services and improve the stability of patient health data management.

The agreement covers converting the eppiday chatbot to a Korean large language model and building domestic AI infrastructure. The answer-generation system behind the platform's "AI health coaching" feature will shift from overseas cloud services to in-house domestic servers running on Korean-made AI chips. Hanmi will first apply the Korean model to the chatbot's answer-generation function, then gradually convert existing drug and dietary information searches and meal photo recognition. Eppiday supports personalized health management based on questionnaires and health data entered by patients, recording daily data such as weight, meals and exercise.

Under the agreement, Hanmi will set the overall business direction and priorities, while Bagel Labs will handle app and chatbot development, AI model replacement and answer quality verification. Xperix will build and operate the domestic AI servers and provide the model inference environment, and FuriosaAI will supply Korean-made AI chips and support model optimization. CEO Hwang Sang-yeon said the agreement is significant because it lays the foundation for processing patient health data more safely and reliably in a sovereign AI environment based on domestic technology. Kim Na-young, executive vice president of Hanmi's innovation and growth division, said the competitiveness of digital health care lies not in adopting technology itself but in delivering consistent quality and real benefits to patients.

The four companies have verified in a test environment that the AI coaching answer-generation function can be moved to domestic in-house servers. They are also comparing answer accuracy and response speed before and after the conversion using a standard problem set and an automated scoring system. The timing of the rollout to the live service will be set after quality and safety verification and further discussions. The four companies plan to run a regular working-level consultative body to share progress on each stage of the conversion and the results of quality verification, and to broaden the application of Korean AI technology in digital health care.

Articles.Title: Hanmi Pharmaceutical Shifts Health App Chatbot to Korean AI - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Samsung Launches 'Samsung Crew' Creator Program for AI Home Appliances
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics launched a creator program called Samsung Crew to showcase real-world experiences with its artificial intelligence home appliances, the company said on Nov. 1. Samsung held an inaugural ceremony for the first class of Samsung Crew on Oct. 30 at CGV's The Private Cinema in Seoul's Cheongdam district, where it shared plans for the program. The first class consists of about 30 creators who have produced lifestyle content on YouTube, Instagram and blogs covering living, interior design, child care and daily life. Over the next three months, they will create content introducing how to use Samsung's AI appliances and what the experience is like in practice.

The creators plan to convey the changes AI appliances bring to daily life from a consumer's perspective, reflecting their own living spaces and lifestyles. Beyond simple product reviews, they will also highlight Samsung's services across the entire process from purchase to use, including delivery, professional installation and after-sales care. The content will be released through the creators' own channels, including YouTube, Instagram and blogs. Samsung will provide the creators with the latest AI appliances suited to their personal tastes and home environments to support their activities.

Samsung will also offer opportunities to attend official brand events, special seminars and class programs. The company plans to support networking activities as well, allowing creators to share tips on connecting appliances to one another and on filming techniques. Samsung said it will build a long-term collaboration framework with the creators following the launch of the first class and reflect their real usage feedback in product and service improvements. Park Jung-mi, executive vice president and head of Samsung Electronics' Korea operations, said the candid experiences of creators who have long cherished and trusted Samsung AI appliances should help more consumers appreciate the convenience and value they bring to daily life. She said Samsung plans to keep developing Samsung Crew and broaden its points of contact with consumers across a wider range of platforms.

Articles.Title: Samsung Launches 'Samsung Crew' Creator Program for AI Home Appliances - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: CEVA Unveils 2nd-Gen NeuPro NPU, Doubling AI Throughput
stories.Summary:
CEVA unveiled its second-generation NeuPro neural processing unit product lineup on Nov. 2, 2026. The company said the new lineup delivers up to twice the AI processing throughput per square millimeter compared with the first generation, while energy efficiency has improved by 50%. CEVA plans to use the product family to expand its business into AI infrastructure, including AI inference semiconductors, intelligent memory, and connectivity chips. The lineup is currently available to select customers for early access, with full production supply scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027.

More than 15 customers have licensed the first-generation NeuPro, and CEVA said work with them helped it identify how much computing performance, memory bandwidth, power consumption, and cost matter for different AI applications. The new lineup therefore offers multiple computing engines for uses ranging from always-on, low-power sensors and edge devices to data centers and other AI infrastructure. All products in the lineup use the same instruction set architecture and a common software development kit, which CEVA said lets customers reuse existing software assets when designing systems that integrate multiple NPUs into a single system-on-chip. The lineup supports workloads from basic object recognition and classification to transformer-based large language models, multimodal AI that understands text, speech, and images, agentic AI that makes decisions and takes actions autonomously, and Physical AI. It also supports FP4 and FP8 floating-point formats along with mixed-precision computing, allowing AI processing precision to be flexibly reduced to improve efficiency.

CEVA said the architecture reduces memory usage and the volume of data transferred within and between chips. It adds a paged key-value cache feature, which manages memory in separate blocks as conversational context grows, and a dynamic tensor shape feature that handles frequently changing input data formats, such as prompts, without performance degradation or memory waste. Tensor reshaping also improves utilization of the chip's multiply-accumulate units. For large AI models, the architecture supports a Mixture-of-Experts structure, which selectively activates expert computing models suited to specific queries, and a linear attention structure designed to analyze long sequences more efficiently.

Articles.Title: CEVA Unveils 2nd-Gen NeuPro NPU, Doubling AI Throughput - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers
stories.Summary:
Zohran Mamdani gave an interview to WIRED at New York’s City Hall about ten months after he became mayor of New York City. WIRED had first interviewed him in October 2025, weeks before his historic election win, at his campaign office. In the new interview, published on November 3, 2026, he spoke about what he has learned on the job, how he uses social media for governance, and where he stands on issues in the midterm elections. The interview notes that his approval rating among city voters is 69 percent.

The interview covers his use of social media as a governing tool rather than only a campaign tool. He said his administration made a WhatsApp channel called El Chisme Oficial de NYC to share information directly with Spanish-speaking New Yorkers, including voice notes of him speaking halting Spanish. He said social media lets the city make a video that will reach more than a million people on one medium alone. He argued that politics must reach people wherever they already are instead of expecting them to find a press release in an obscure place. He also said that putting tired, old ideas into a short-form vertical video does not answer the critical issue with politics today.

The interview also addresses the distinction between professional journalism and content creation, after The New York Times published a story in September about his office’s work with creators. Some creators receive talking points around initiatives and are invited to cover events, sometimes where traditional journalists would not be present. Mamdani said talking points are essentially the basis of a press release, which includes quotes and a description of the policy. He said that if his administration engaged exclusively with digital-first creators, that would be an issue, but he sees it as important to speak to journalists across television, newspaper, radio, digital and magazine. He also described a recent announcement about lowering water levels in three key water bodies in Central Park to prevent storm water runoff ahead of a storm.

The interview describes his year as transformative, and he said leading the city is the greatest job in the world. He said that at 35, most people in his work are significantly older than him, so the meaning of his age does not really live in a professional setting. He recalled that Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was excited by his youth when they met during the UN General Assembly. He said being 35 means he grew up through the housing crisis and the Iraq War, formative moments that shaped his politics. The interview does not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers

stories.Headline: LS Electric Chairman Koo Ja-kyun Outlines AI Power Grid Vision
stories.Summary:
LS Electric Chairman Koo Ja-kyun gave a keynote address on next-generation power grids at the 2026 International Conference on Electricity Distribution Workshop, held at JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square Seoul on Nov. 2, the company said. He said power grids must become more reliable to ensure stable operations of AI data centers, while AI should also be used to manage electricity networks more efficiently. He described a virtuous cycle between Grids for AI, which supplies power to AI infrastructure, and AI for Grids, which uses AI to manage power networks. He identified direct current and intelligent platforms as key technologies for next-generation power grids.

Koo called for moving beyond conventional one-way electricity supply systems and building infrastructure that combines alternating current and direct current to meet the specific requirements of customers, including data centers. He said data and AI must be integrated into power equipment so that grids become intelligent, bidirectional energy platforms that can detect abnormalities early and flexibly exchange energy. LS Electric is expanding its business in North America by supplying power conversion systems and power solutions for data centers. As electricity consumption by AI data centers increases, power distribution equipment and power conversion technologies are becoming increasingly important, according to the article.

Koo is the chairman of LS Electric, and the article attributes the vision to him and reports his remarks from the keynote. The article does not say who else is responsible for carrying out the changes or give any further statements from the company. It also gives no timeline beyond the Nov. 2 event and no specific targets or figures for the grid plans. The context is the growing electricity demand from AI data centers, which the article says makes power distribution equipment and power conversion technologies increasingly important.

Articles.Title: LS Electric Chairman Koo Ja-kyun Outlines AI Power Grid Vision - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: Taiwanese UMC Secures Major Orders from Chinese Firms for AI Optical Chips
stories.Summary:
Taiwanese foundry UMC has secured orders for up to 10,000 wafers of optical communication semiconductors, according to the Taiwan Economic Daily on Nov. 2. The orders for photonic integrated circuits, or PICs, come from Zhongji Innolight, an optical communication equipment company, and SILITH, a chip design company backed by China's Tencent. The initial combined volume from the two firms is expected to reach up to 10,000 wafers, with production planned at UMC's Singapore plant. Additional orders are also being discussed.

A PIC is a chip that transmits data using light rather than electrical signals, and such chips are essential in AI data centers where many servers exchange data at once. Transmission speeds in these centers are rising from the 800Gbps class to 1.6Tbps, with 3.2Tbps expected later. UMC and SILITH said they began first mass production of PICs at a 12-inch plant in Singapore in July, about 18 months after development started. SILITH's cumulative shipments of 100G and 200G class PICs have reportedly exceeded 8,000,000 units.

UMC said during its earnings presentation last month that it had completed verification of its 1.6T optical communication technology for several large cloud companies. The company plans to raise transmission speeds further and apply technology that precisely combines multiple semiconductors. In July it announced it would add production space and equipment at its P4 plant in Singapore and build a new factory building in Tainan, Taiwan. The local industry expects UMC's PIC capacity to reach 18,000 wafers per month in the long term.

Taiwanese industry estimates put the average selling price of some high-performance PIC wafers at about seven times that of regular CMOS wafers, though this is an estimate and not confirmed by UMC. The report said few companies can mass-produce optical communication semiconductors, and capacity at major producers Tower Semiconductor and GlobalFoundries is also short of spare room. Related equipment is expected to be introduced starting at the end of 2028, with full-scale operations around 2030. Some large customers have reportedly begun talks to secure production volumes in advance.

Articles.Title: Taiwanese UMC Secures Major Orders from Chinese Firms for AI Optical Chips - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: SK hynix Q4 Operating Profit Seen Surpassing 100 Trillion Won for First Time
stories.Summary:
KB Securities said on Nov. 2 that SK hynix is expected to post a record quarterly operating profit of 104 trillion won in the fourth quarter of 2026. The brokerage said this would be the first time the company's quarterly operating profit has exceeded 100 trillion won. It also estimated that SK hynix posted an operating profit of 83 trillion won in the third quarter, with an operating margin of about 80%, the company's highest quarterly earnings on record. The fourth-quarter figure would be up 441% from a year earlier, and the operating margin is expected to reach a record 83%.

KB Securities maintained its Buy rating on SK hynix and kept its target price at 3.5 million won, or about $2,616.24. Analyst Kim Dong-won said the stock trades at just three times its projected earnings for next year and has fallen about 50% from its peak. He said the combination of record earnings and deep undervaluation is an opportunity for a valuation recovery. The report said annual operating profit is forecast to reach 285 trillion won in 2026 and 470 trillion won in 2027, up 504% and 65% respectively from the previous year.

The earnings growth is driven by higher shipment volumes and average selling prices for DRAM and NAND flash memory. KB Securities projected that DRAM and NAND bit shipments would rise 24% and 5% respectively from the previous quarter in the fourth quarter. The share of high-bandwidth memory sales accounted for by HBM4 is also expected to surpass that of HBM3E. The report cited long-term supply agreements and advance volume commitments as key factors improving earnings visibility, with more than 50% of total memory production capacity for 2027 and 2028 allocated under five-year supply agreements and planned DRAM and HBM volumes through 2029 effectively sold out.

SK hynix is also moving ahead with a shareholder return program worth approximately 100 trillion won. The plan includes 60 trillion won in treasury-share cancellations and more than 30 trillion won in cash dividends, making it the largest such program on record. Kim said the expansion of the shareholder return policy will mark a decisive turning point in narrowing the gap between corporate value and the share price. He added that with DRAM prices expected to rise 40% next year, fourth-quarter earnings are likely to mark the beginning of a new phase of profit growth. SK hynix shares were trading at 1,369,000 won on Nextrade on Nov. 2, down 3.46% from the previous session, amid a sell-off following disappointing earnings from global technology companies including Amazon and Intel.

Articles.Title: SK hynix Q4 Operating Profit Seen Surpassing 100 Trillion Won for First Time - Businesskorea

The move comes in response to surging demand for optical communications driven by AI and data center expansion. The report was written by Jenchieh Chiang of Taipei.

stories.Headline: For Government, PHP Scare Points to an AI-Fueled New Normal
stories.Summary:
Websites around the world went down last week, including pages for Australia's national cyber defense agency, the Netherlands' national digital identity service and the Paris police. The outages were not a hack but an emergency precaution after two critical flaws were announced in PHP, a programming language used in roughly 70 percent of websites. Researchers used AI to help find one of the bugs in August, and AI also helped show how the other bug, known to the organization behind PHP since 2024, could be exploited. Michael Klein of the Institute for Security and Technology said hackers who leverage the flaws could shut down or alter websites or access private information.

The PHP Foundation, the almost-entirely volunteer team that maintains the language, released a patch for the two vulnerabilities on Oct. 21. Either flaw could let hackers access IT systems without a login, and a patch is available at least for more recent versions of the software. About half of Internet-connected PHP software runs older versions for which there is currently no patch, though patches may be in the works for some and others may never be fixed. Japan's prime minister urged website operators to apply patches as soon as possible, and the FBI advised anyone who could not immediately patch to take their sites offline until they could.

John Matelski, CIO and managing director of the National Association of Counties, told Governing on Monday that none of the counties he is in touch with had reported a breach. On Friday, the federal Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said it was unaware of anyone successfully using the vulnerabilities to hack an organization. Klein said a vendor released word of the patches a few days early, which leaked the existence of the flaws and sparked a flurry of unsuccessful hacking attempts. He said AI can take a weakness that was only theoretical and turn it into a working attack, which changes how vulnerabilities are viewed.

Governments that had inventoried all the software they or their vendors run knew quickly whether they were at risk, and those with plans prioritizing security fixes did not have to work that out on the fly. Matelski said this will not be the last time governments must spring into action over new vulnerabilities, so getting the right process in place now matters. That includes a careful process for applying patches, then checking the updates worked and did not disrupt other processes. Klein said governments can prepare with tabletop exercises, including deciding who decides whether to take down a site, and with plans for communicating with constituents and for how long to keep a site offline.

Articles.Title: For Government, PHP Scare Points to an AI-Fueled New Normal

stories.Headline: Unlocking the AI-native digital brand
stories.Summary:
A white paper titled Unlocking the AI-native digital brand was published by TM Forum on 3 November 2026, sponsored by the software company Etiya. It is a research report on artificial intelligence, offered as a download in exchange for contact details. The paper argues that launching a greenfield digital brand lets a company reach new customer segments, innovate quickly and open new revenue streams. It is aimed at firms whose main brand is held back by legacy infrastructure, price competition or flat subscriber numbers.

The paper says a purpose-built platform can run a fully operational, AI-powered digital brand separately from an existing BSS stack, the systems telecom operators use to manage customers and billing. According to the article, this setup lets a company deliver hyper-personalized services, engage customers proactively, cut time-to-market, lower operational costs and raise ARPU, or average revenue per user. Etiya describes a greenfield digital sub-brand as the fastest path to new growth for a constrained primary brand. The download form states that contact information, including email address, will be shared with the sponsor.

The article names Joanne Taaffe as Editor in Chief and Richard Mahoney as Commercial Director for Research, Events and Media at TM Forum. It presents the paper as a sponsored research report from Etiya, and the download page asks users to consent to marketing communications from TM Forum and from Etiya. The article does not include direct comments from named executives. It says people can update their email subscription preferences at any time and points to a privacy policy for details on how data is processed.

The context given is that some primary brands are limited by legacy infrastructure, price competition or subscriber stagnation. For those companies, the article presents a separate digital brand on an AI-native operating model as a way to grow, built for speed, scale and differentiation. The article says the white paper explains how new digital brands bring incremental growth opportunities. stories.Headline: Why HR AI Needs Rules, Not Just Reasoning
stories.Summary:
Leigh Elena Henderson, who has worked more than 20 years in corporate HR, wrote a sponsored article published by Harvard Business Review on November 2, 2026, arguing that AI in HR needs rules as well as reasoning. She said AI in HR once stayed in the shallow end, updating job descriptions and drafting policy documents, but it is now moving into hiring, payroll, compliance, performance management and workforce planning. She wrote that mistakes in these areas go beyond typos and can damage trust with employees. She described the pressure on HR leaders as coming from every direction at once, with the CEO wanting speed, the CFO wanting savings and legal wanting zero exposure. The article cites Workday's 2026 research, which surveyed 6,100 professionals across HR, finance, IT and operations who actively use AI.

It says 87 percent agreed that AI increases their confidence in decisions only when they trust the underlying systems and data. It says 81 percent said their organization relies on a small number of trusted systems to determine what is true when the stakes are high, as with pay, compliance, reporting or audits. It also says HR respondents were more likely than the global average, 68 percent versus 64 percent, to say different teams often disagree about whose numbers are correct. Henderson draws a distinction between lawless AI, which sits outside context and gives a confident answer without knowing whether the person asking is allowed to act on it or whether the data is current, and lawful AI, which is grounded in systems of record, rules and security. She quotes a global manufacturing company's SVP and CHRO saying that AI can provide the recommendation but the human needs to be in the driver's seat to make the decision.

She lists checks for a CHRO evaluating an AI product, including whether it operates within enterprise permissions, understands role, policy and workflow context, routes through the right approvals, keeps an audit trail, draws from trusted systems of record and maintains human judgment and accountability. She says that if the answer to any of those is not sure, the organization has an experiment rather than an AI strategy. Henderson writes that trust should be integrated from the beginning rather than tacked on to a solution, and that for most organizations the beginning is right now. She says the organizations that successfully integrate AI into HR will not be those that deploy the most tools or pilots, but those that embed AI into the systems where trust, context and accountability already live. The article is sponsor content from Workday and includes a link on how Workday can help organizations put AI to work with trust, context and governance.

Articles.Title: Why HR AI Needs Rules, Not Just Reasoning

stories.Headline: Palm Beach plane crash footage isn’t AI-generated, despite social media claims
stories.Summary:
A business jet, a Learjet 60, crashed into a neighborhood near Cresthaven, Florida, at about 12:51 p.m. ET on Nov. 1, 2026, while headed to the Bahamas from Austin, Texas. Everyone on board died, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that day. Footage of the plane nosediving into the ground, cratering the pavement and dissolving into fire and smoke was shared by The Associated Press, CNN, CBS News and BBC. Its original source was Aki Kuusisto, a digital creator from West Palm Beach, who first posted the clip on Facebook and said in the comments that this was not quite what he had in mind when he installed the dash cam.

Some social media users claimed the footage was fake, including a Nov. 1 X post saying the video was 100% AI generated and that someone was lying. The posts showed screen recordings of the clip being run through Hive Moderation, an AI-detection tool, which reported detecting AI-generated content. PolitiFact said Hive Moderation is an imperfect tool, and when it ran Kuusisto's footage through the tool, it did not flag it as AI-generated or manipulated. Authorities have not said what caused the crash, but Tom Chapman of the National Transportation Safety Board said on Nov. 2 that the aircraft experienced turbulence and encountered ice.

Timothy Monville, who is leading the investigation for the safety board, said the agency has just begun documenting the incident and has a lot of work to do on scene. He said it will be a several-day process and the biggest obstacle will be recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway. Darren Linvill, co-director of the Media Forensics Hub at Clemson University, told PolitiFact that people are right to be skeptical of viral videos as AI improves, but some have grown so distrustful that they disbelieve the truth, a phenomenon known as the liar's dividend. He said that is what is occurring with the video of the Palm Beach crash and that people should get their news from reliable sources. PolitiFact noted that one of the X accounts that questioned the footage has been amplified by bot accounts promoting narratives by Russian Storm-1516, and it rated the claim Pants on Fire.

Articles.Title: Palm Beach plane crash footage isn’t AI-generated, despite social media claims

stories.Headline: OpenAI executive urges caution in China-US AI talks, warns of distillation
stories.Summary:
Caroline Zier, OpenAI’s deputy lead for national security, spoke on Monday at a discussion at the Hudson Institute in Washington. She said Washington needs to be clear-eyed and aware about sharing information with Beijing during coming talks on artificial intelligence. She also warned about the threat posed by alleged Chinese distillation attacks. Zier served as a special assistant to the US secretary of defence from 2021 to 2023.

Zier endorsed the bilateral dialogue between the United States and China on AI. She expressed scepticism that Washington and Beijing share the same understanding of the risks involved. She advised being very clear-eyed and very aware of what information you are able to expect in return for what you are sharing. She said the two sides should start to build a foundation.

stories.Headline: California campaigns are turning to content creators and AI. What does that mean for voters?
stories.Summary:
The race to become California's next governor has raised questions about how campaigns reach voters online, through paid social media influencers and AI-generated attack ads. The dispute over paid influencers became a talking point during the primary when billionaire Tom Steyer's campaign was scrutinized for paying creators to post favorable content about him, and complaints were filed with the California Fair Political Practices Commission because some posts did not disclose the payments. Steyer's campaign also filed a complaint alleging that two pro-Becerra creators, including Jordan "Jay" Gonzalez, had failed to disclose payments from Becerra's campaign. Becerra's campaign denied paying outside creators for undisclosed political content, and Gonzalez said he had not been paid for the content in question, though he added disclosures to some earlier posts after joining the campaign as a full-time social media strategist in April. Republican nominee Steve Hilton has frequently used AI-generated videos in ads attacking Becerra, including one where Becerra is auctioned off to utility companies, oil executives and large unions, and his campaign added disclosures saying the videos were generated or substantially altered using AI.

A new state law takes effect in January and is intended to strengthen enforcement of disclosure requirements for paid political influencer advertising. Adam Silver, chair of the California Fair Political Practices Commission, said the law will create administrative and civil liability for both the campaign paying an influencer and the influencer who fails to include a required disclaimer, and it requires more specific reporting of campaign spending on influencers so regulators, journalists and the public can identify those payments and check whether posts include the required disclosures. Silver said he is also concerned about "trend simulation," when multiple creators are paid to share specific clips to make a message appear to be spreading organically, and he wants the commission to have tools to identify the practice. He said California law does not require a disclaimer for every use of AI, and he wants state agencies to work with social media platforms to identify and address misleading content faster than regulators can investigate individual complaints.

Becerra's spokesperson Jonathan Underland said the campaign's focus after the June primary was building a coalition and raising money, and that it has since made more time for interviews, describing a natural lull in campaign activity during the summer. He said the campaign has tried to broaden outreach by giving creators time to ask questions at public events alongside traditional news organizations. Jason Turcotte, chair of the communications department at Cal Poly Pomona, said he is not opposed to candidates appearing with influencers but worries about replacing traditional news access with digital and social media, which he said is a loss for the public because journalists are trained to hold candidates accountable. Comedian Sophia Garrow, who interviewed both candidates for The San Francisco Standard, said neither campaign restricted her questions, and she cautioned that voters should not put all their trust in content creators. Political content creator Eric Cheng said the Becerra campaign for the most part did not control his questions or posts, and he predicted creators will play an even larger role in covering campaigns.

Articles.Title: California campaigns are turning to content creators and AI. What does that mean for voters?

stories.Headline: Tom Lee Calls Bottom on AI Stock Selloff, Citing Tight Supply and Crypto Resilience
stories.Summary:
Tom Lee, the co-founder of Fundstrat and chairman of Bitmine, said in a CNBC interview on Squawk Box that the AI stock selloff has reached its bottom. He said he thinks we are at the bottom, and he acknowledged that bottoms are dangerous because you do not know how much more downside you have. His call came as the decline spread beyond individual AI companies, with large technology stocks also sitting inside the funds many people use to invest for retirement. The interview aired on Monday, November 2, 2026.

Lee argued that the market for AI is still very tight and not an overcapacity market. He said constraints on spending, including political opposition, are slowing growth without signaling that the boom has peaked. He also pointed to crypto's limited response to the Binance security breach, which the exchange initially estimated had an impact of about $6.3 billion. In his reading, a market that absorbs bad news without a much larger decline may have fewer sellers left to push prices down.

Intel offered a sharp example on Friday, when its shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 after a disappointing fourth-quarter forecast. Its data center and AI revenue had risen 78% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, yet manufacturing constraints limited its ability to meet demand. Intel projected quarterly revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, with the midpoint about $1.6 billion below analysts' expectations. Its weaker PC business added pressure, showing why healthy AI demand can coexist with a falling share price.

Bitcoin fell about 4% to roughly $76,400 on Friday, and more than $1.3 billion in positions funded with borrowed money were forcibly closed. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds shed $643.2 million that day, their largest daily outflow of October. Binance said on Friday that about $3 billion of the affected assets had been frozen and pledged to cover losses using its emergency reserve and company funds. The article does not say what happens next beyond those statements.

Articles.Title: Tom Lee Calls Bottom on AI Stock Selloff, Citing Tight Supply and Crypto Resilience

stories.Headline: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex
stories.Summary:
Qodo, a startup that builds AI tools for code review and software quality, created a plugin for the Codex marketplace, OpenAI said in an article published on November 2, 2026. The plugin gives Codex access to codebase knowledge, organizational rules and independent review through Qodo's Agentic Toolbox. Qodo uses OpenAI models including GPT-6 Astra to gather engineering knowledge, review code and monitor software quality. Co-founder and CEO Itamar Friedman said Qodo is the coding agent's best friend.

The plugin is meant for customer environments that can span 10,000 or more repositories, where a local change can break a downstream service even if it looks correct on its own. With the added context, Codex can account for dependencies across repositories, including those hosted by different Git providers or connected through Kafka. Before writing code, Codex can use the plugin to retrieve relevant codebase rules and pull request history and patterns. After Codex makes changes, Qodo reviews them and returns findings in the same session, before the developer opens a pull request.

Friedman said Qodo loves OpenAI models and wants the frontier reasoning models but also ones that are really fast. He described coding and review agents as yin and yang, with one creating code and the other challenging it, and said that is how trust is created. Nnenna Ndukwe, Qodo's AI Developer Relations Lead, said she has seen developers use the workflow to build features and tackle technical debt with GPT-6 models in Codex. She said the process lets people leverage the best parts of their expertise.

Friedman also sees an opportunity to use OpenAI's recently launched Decisions API to choose which rules and agent skills apply at each stage of development. He gave an example where the API could select which of 200 rules need checking before a language model reasons through the relevant ones, making selection faster and cheaper. Ndukwe said Qodo's approach combines the best aspects of artificial intelligence with the best aspects of traditional software engineering and scripting. Friedman described the foundation of a software factory, a system customers could assemble and own, bringing coding and review agents together with an understanding of how software changes in production.

Articles.Title: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex

stories.Headline: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens
stories.Summary:
Garry Tan, the CEO of Y Combinator, said he spends about $100,000 to $200,000 a year on tokens for AI agents. He made the remark on a new episode of Walter Isaacson’s podcast The Builders, which was set to publish on Tuesday. The article was published by TechCrunch on November 2, 2026, and written by Julie Bort. Tan has in the past jokingly admitted to “cyber psychosis” and sometimes barely sleeps because he is so excited to work with his agents.

Tan uses agents for many work projects and coding tasks, and he has shared a set of 23 Claude Code skills called gstack on GitHub to help teach others what agents can do. He uses his agent to research the podcast and prep for questions, and also to help run his life. He said the agent has read all of his email, all of his Dropbox and all of his Apple Notes, including therapy notes going back 20 years. He described an agent as a Jiminy Cricket on your shoulder that knows you and can run ahead and help you see around corners.

Tan said he has learned not to treat AI agents like traditional software, because some people worry so much about repeatability and safety that they trade off the good parts of working with an agent. He said Y Combinator has an internal AI agent named Stray Light that has a personality and a company brain with the total context of every founder YC has backed, everyone who has emailed it and all the applications. He said the agent is rebuilding the way YC operates. He also said he knows his spending is a crazy privilege that not everyone can do.

Tan believes personal AI agents will become mainstream if one major problem is solved, which is that costs have to come down, and he said it is too expensive right now. He suggested free agents controlled by Big Tech may not be the answer either. He said Meta is a huge company that controls the algorithm and that we all wish at some level that it did not. He said you could imagine a personal AI that you control and program.

Articles.Title: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens

stories.Headline: AI measurements of heart scans more strongly linked to patient survival than clinician measurements
stories.Summary:
Researchers led by City St George's, University of London and University College London compared AI measurements of heart function from MRI scans with measurements made by experienced clinicians. The study, published in The Lancet Digital Health, analyzed scans from 27,382 patients in the U.K. and United States who were being investigated for known or suspected heart conditions. Patients were followed for an average of more than five years, and 3,458 deaths occurred during that time. The team found that AI-derived measurements of ejection fraction were slightly but significantly better at predicting which patients were at increased risk of death. The findings held after accounting for factors such as age and sex.

Ejection fraction describes how effectively the heart pumps blood and is widely used to guide treatment decisions for people with heart disease. It helps doctors decide on specialist heart failure treatments, implanted heart devices and procedures to improve blood flow, and it is used to gauge surgical risk and monitor heart function during chemotherapy. The AI tool analyzed scans in approximately 2 to 3 seconds per patient, compared with around 13 minutes for expert clinician analysis in previous work by the team. AI errors were uncommon, with an error rate of around 1% at the patient level affecting just 0.08% of images.

Dr. George Joy, lead author and NIHR clinical lecturer at City St George's, said ejection fraction is one of the most important measurements in cardiology because it helps determine how patients are treated and how closely they are monitored. He said the findings suggest AI can measure this marker with remarkable consistency and precision, giving a small but meaningful improvement in identifying higher-risk patients. Dr. Rhodri Davies, senior author and inventor of the AI tool, said even modest improvements in accuracy can have a significant impact across thousands of patients. He said AI is not replacing clinicians but can provide faster, more consistent measurements at low cost and support more streamlined decision-making.

The researchers stress that human oversight remains essential, and clinicians should still verify results and interpret scans within the broader clinical context. The findings support using AI as a first-line tool for analyzing cardiac MRI scans, with expert review where needed. As health care systems face increasing demand, the technology could help reduce workloads while maintaining high standards of care and helping patients receive lifesaving treatments sooner. The team now plans to combine AI measurements from heart scans with those from other tests, particularly electrocardiograms, to spot problems in the heart muscle earlier so treatment can begin before lasting damage occurs.

Articles.Title: AI measurements of heart scans more strongly linked to patient survival than clinician measurements

stories.Headline: A lasting AI sell-off is one of the biggest risks to the economy, BofA warns
stories.Summary:
BofA Global Research economists warned in a report on Monday, November 2, 2026, that a lasting sell-off in AI stocks is one of the larger risks to the US and global economy. The warning came after AI stocks lost about $5 trillion in market value over three weeks. The Nasdaq 100 ended the previous Friday about 9% below its October 6 record, though stocks were rebounding early Monday. Hedge funds have already pulled back from the AI trade.

The report said a sustained correction would hit growth directly through spending and indirectly through the wealth effect, where falling stock prices make households feel poorer and spend less. Investment in computers, information-processing equipment and software added more than 1 percentage point to third quarter GDP growth of 3.4%, about a third of the total, per Yahoo Finance calculations using Bureau of Economic Analysis data. Stocks made up a record 48% of Americans' financial assets in the second quarter, according to Federal Reserve data going back to 1945, topping the 39% peak of the dot-com bubble. The richest 10% of households own 88% of stocks. Hedge funds are underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023, according to Morgan Stanley prime brokerage data, though their sensitivity to the Magnificent Seven was in the 97th percentile of its history as of October 26, according to a Nomura note.

BofA's economists said growth now reaches well beyond AI, with the economy growing more than 2% last quarter without AI-related spending, up from about 1% at the start of the year. They wrote that it is hard to justify the Fed's inaction given growth running hot for years, and that borrowing to fund AI and higher interest rates are tied together. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said at his October 28 press conference that interest rates get in the cracks and affect directly or indirectly almost everything. On Monday, Oracle launched a $10 billion bond sale alongside a $10 billion stock offering, Reuters reported, and Alphabet began its second euro bond sale this year. Oracle stock fell Monday morning.

Articles.Title: A lasting AI sell-off is one of the biggest risks to the economy, BofA warns

stories.Headline: 7 sure-fire ways to blow your AI budget
stories.Summary:
CIOs have long faced pressure to deploy emerging technologies quickly, and AI is following the same pattern. Many CIOs bought enterprise-wide AI model licenses and let employees experiment with language models and build AI agents. Others pushed DevOps teams to speed up AI code generation. Moving from rapid experimentation to production can leave CIOs with mounting AI debt and gaps in AI financial management. The article lists seven common mistakes that blow AI budgets.

It cites a Collibra and Harris Poll finding that 96% of IT leaders say project failure almost always traces back to poor data foundations, and 51% report significant staff hours spent manually fixing autonomous AI agent outputs. It cites a Stack Overflow 2026 Developer Survey finding that 73% of developers use AI coding assistants and agents daily, and that developers care more about quality, at 75%, than cost, at 38%. It also cites a Sonar survey finding that 96% of developers do not fully trust AI-generated code and 48% always check AI-assisted code before committing, and a Databricks figure that 77% of companies now juggle multiple model families. Rob Scudiere, CTO at Verint, said every token spent on a pilot that never proves its value is money leaders cannot get back, and that every agent and workflow should earn its budget by showing business results or lose it. Kris Beevers, CEO and cofounder of Netbox Labs, said that if adoption is climbing but outcomes are not moving with it, that is a good signal to rethink spending.

Guy Bourgault of Concentrix said delayed AI governance is framed as a compliance risk but is just as much a budgetary concern. Varun Goswami of Newgen recommended building on one governed platform rather than a dozen parallel stacks and matching the model to the job. Prakash Kota, CIO at UKG, described a Three T's test of talent, tools, and tokens. Tom Shea of OneStream said the same tokens can go to a skilled engineer shipping faster or to a non-expert generating ten versions of the same slide deck. Anurag Dhingra of Cisco said coding is no longer the constraint and the bottleneck has moved to ensuring code correctness.

Andrea Malagodi of Sonar said teams need clear guardrails and engineering standards. Craig Wiley of Databricks said the fix is real-time budgets and smart routing to the most cost-effective model. Josh Fecteau of Teradata recommended diversifying with cheaper small language models and custom models. CJ Combs of Columbus said AI costs stop being predictable once an agent can loop. Babak Pahlavan of NinjaTech AI said a single agent running a multi-hour task can burn a month's allocation in an afternoon.

Adi Elimelech of Jedify said token costs can scale with the size of the environment rather than the complexity of the question. The article's recommendations include setting financial objectives before agents move into development and deployment, and updating AI governance policies monthly. It suggests partnering with the CFO to measure total impact, including token costs, employee effort, inference costs, and value delivered, and setting budgets at the employee, department, and workflow levels. It advises establishing financial targets on a maturity curve, encouraging experimentation first and fiscal discipline once agents reach production. It also says CIOs should set guidelines for balancing cost and quality in code generation and mature AgenticOps and site reliability engineering practices to monitor agents and respond to cost, security, quality, and performance incidents.

Articles.Title: 7 sure-fire ways to blow your AI budget

stories.Headline: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps
stories.Summary:
Apple signaled on its earnings call on Monday, November 2, 2026, that it may look to boost services revenue through third-party apps, according to TechCrunch. Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh said AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch, and that there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party ones. He did not elaborate on what those opportunities might be. Reuters reported that investors are wondering whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through the App Store and taking a cut of the revenue they generate.

Apple's services business remains at record levels but is facing growing pressure, and its App Store has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming. Regulatory and legal changes have cut into App Store commission revenue in some markets, and third-party estimates in August suggested an 18% drop in U.S. commission revenue, with declines also in Brazil and Japan after new regulations there. A lawsuit by Epic Games forced Apple to allow apps to redirect users to outside payment systems. Parekh said App Store performance in the September quarter was similar to the prior year, with a record number of paid subscriptions and double-digit growth for third-party apps.

Parekh said Apple expects services growth of 8 to 9% in the December quarter, an outlook that contemplates headwinds primarily from third-party licensing and an additional half percentage point of foreign exchange. He said Apple saw headwinds in mobile gaming and expects them to continue into the summer quarter. TechCrunch said it had reached out to Apple for more information and would update the story if the company responds. The articles do not say what specific plans, if any, Apple has for third-party AI apps.

Articles.Title: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps

stories.Headline: Election Policy Landscape Stabilizes as Midterms Approach—Part 4: AI and Elections
stories.Summary:
The 2026 midterm election is the second major election cycle since artificial intelligence entered the mainstream and AI tools became widely available to the public. Concerns that the technology could disrupt the 2024 presidential election turned out to be unfounded, but questions remain about its role in 2026. The current environment differs because of rapid advances in technological capabilities, the increased use of AI tools in daily life, and a rise in government regulation of deceptive uses of AI in election communications. Chris McIsaac wrote the analysis for the R Street Institute, published on November 2, 2026, as the final installment in a multipart series on the election policy landscape.

A Pew survey conducted in mid-October found that only 8 percent of Americans currently turn to AI chatbots with questions about the election. A larger share is likely to receive election information from AI tools, since 6 in 10 Americans report reading the AI-generated summary at the top of search results. One study from the Institute for Strategic Dialogue found a 29 percent error rate in election-related responses from six popular chatbots. According to one estimate, campaigns and political action committees have spent over $137 million on 220 advertisements created or enhanced by AI during this election cycle.

Thirty-one states now regulate AI-generated election deepfakes, and 29 of those laws were enacted in 2023 or later. Most of the state laws require creators of misleading election-related deepfakes to label the videos as AI-generated, with penalties ranging from civil fines to years in jail depending on the state. Legal challenges in California, Hawaii, Montana, and Vermont have already succeeded in blocking their implementation, with federal judges determining that they likely violate the First Amendment. The article argues that a better approach is for the government to let the public engage in free speech without imposing labeling requirements that could be unconstitutional and counterproductive.

The 2026 election will be the first test for these laws in many states. Amid the growing use of AI by campaigns this cycle, there will likely be more opportunities for the subject of a deepfake to file a complaint or for the government to prosecute someone who violates the law. The article says the impacts of these developments remain to be seen, though the 2026 cycle clearly represents the embrace of AI as a powerful tool in the American electoral process. It concludes that Americans should be trusted to adapt to the new technology and develop innovative solutions that will strengthen American democracy.

Articles.Title: Election Policy Landscape Stabilizes as Midterms Approach—Part 4: AI and Elections

stories.Headline: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
stories.Summary:
Trajectory, a startup founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, announced on November 2, 2026 that it raised $45 million in a Series A round. The round was led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures, at a $300 million valuation. The 18-person company built a platform that lets businesses connect an open source AI model to their applications so it can collect feedback on how the model performs. Trajectory then uses that information to retrain the model, helping it improve at specialized tasks over time. The company is now making its post-training platform publicly available.

Trajectory's approach is known as continual learning, and it aims to spare businesses the cost of hiring internal research teams or expensive consultants, often called forward-deployed engineers, to fine-tune general models. With Trajectory, lawyers, doctors, and other specialists can improve the models near automatically themselves, according to co-founder Ronak Malde. Companies like Harvey and Rogo are already using the platform to post-train open source models so they perform more like experienced lawyers or financial analysts. Trajectory's other customers include Decagon, Mercor, and Nvidia.

Malde compared foundational models to a very smart PhD student who is always starting a new job, while what the economy values is someone who has worked on the job for 30 years. He said the people using Trajectory decide what good looks like for their organization and can turn that into improvements for their model. Co-founder Michael Elabd argued that keeping humans involved in the training process makes Trajectory's approach safer than autonomous self-improvement, which could lead to unintended or even dangerous outcomes. Malde said the startup's biggest advantage is its team, which includes researchers and product designers recruited from OpenAI, Stripe, and Netflix. Co-founder Arjun Karanam said the startup developed an interface that makes post-training more accessible to its nontechnical customers.

Trajectory considers Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and the company behind the fine-tuning platform Tinker, a direct competitor, along with Applied Compute, which was valued at $3.25 billion last month, and Prime Intellect. Separately, The Hindu reported on November 3, 2026 that credible studies have shown that querying an AI model with anonymised data to extract personal details it memorised during training can be used to identify individuals and build their profiles. The article said the right to privacy is a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in 2017, but current legal instruments seem inadequate. It said the Digital Personal Data Protection Act was passed in 2023, with the Rules notified in November 2025, and implementation is phased with some provisions on consent and safety becoming effective only in 2027. Before that Act, the Information Technology Act, 2000 and its 2011 Rules regulated sensitive personal data, with a criminal penalty for unauthorised disclosure capped at three years' imprisonment or a fine of ₹5 lakh.

Articles.Title: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts

stories.Headline: [Call for Writing] How Did AI Change the Way You Worked This Year?
stories.Summary:
JD Supra Perspectives, a publication on JD Supra, issued a call for writing on November 2, 2026, asking legal marketing and business development professionals to share one specific way artificial intelligence changed their work this year. The call came from Laura Gutierrez and Adrian Lurssen. It is part of a special year-end series, and selected responses will be published throughout December in JD Supra's Perspectives channel. The publication said it wants to spotlight big changes, small improvements, surprises and lessons learned.

The call asks four questions of each person who responds. It asks for one way AI changed the person's job in 2026, including the name of the AI tools used, and for a description of one particular task, responsibility or part of the work that changed. It also asks how the work was handled before AI, including the time, effort or coordination it typically required, and how the work is handled now, walking through the new workflow and where AI helps. Finally, it asks for one thing learned from the change, such as a surprise, a limitation, an unexpected benefit or advice for someone doing similar work.

Responses can be sent to Gutierrez or Lurssen, or submitted through a Google Form that includes the option to share an experience anonymously. The publication is collecting responses through the end of November, specifically Monday, November 30, 2026. After that, JD Supra will publish selected responses throughout December. The call states that a person does not need a groundbreaking story, just a real example of how AI has changed their work.

Articles.Title: [Call for Writing] How Did AI Change the Way You Worked This Year?

stories.Headline: Are you using generative AI to help decide who to vote for this election season?
stories.Summary:
Some people have said on social media that they are using ChatGPT to help decide who to vote for in the midterm elections, according to a WSLS 10 report published on November 2, 2026. The report was written by Miles Reese, a community journalist for WSLS 10. The article says AI has been a big conversation for some time and has sparked a national conversation about its use when researching information about midterm candidates. The story appeared under the question of whether readers are using generative AI to help decide who to vote for this election season.

Carole Tarrant, the Communications Director for The League of Women Voters of the Greater Roanoke Valley, cautioned against using ChatGPT in that way. She said midterms are too important to spend five minutes asking a chat who to vote for. She also said the chats are not developed to really give people accurate information. The article gives no other numbers, dates or names beyond the November 2, 2026 publication date, Reese and Tarrant.

Tarrant is the person the article holds responsible for the warning, and the comments are paraphrased from her statements to WSLS 10. The article does not say what tools, other than ChatGPT, people mentioned. It does not give any examples of what the chats told voters. It also does not say whether the League of Women Voters of the Greater Roanoke Valley plans any steps of its own.

The context is the midterm election season, with the article noting that Virginians will decide on several ballot questions, including constitutional protections for abortion and reproductive health care and whether felons should automatically regain the right to vote after release. The article does not say what happens next beyond Tarrant's warning. It does not say whether WSLS 10 will follow up on the social media posts. It does not say how many people said they were using ChatGPT this way.

Articles.Title: Are you using generative AI to help decide who to vote for this election season?

stories.Headline: MEDICAL MONDAY: How AI is being utilized in medical field
stories.Summary:
Dr. Hassan Murshed, a radiation oncologist at Hope Regional Cancer Center in Panama City, Florida, described how artificial intelligence is being used in medical care in an article published by WJHG on November 2, 2026.
