stories.Headline: Ex-Kakao AI executive named head of public AI services task force
stories.Summary:
Kim Se-woong, a former Kakao executive who oversaw AI synergy initiatives, has been appointed to lead a government task force developing artificial intelligence services for the public. The Ministry of Science and ICT said on Monday that it had named Kakao's former vice president as head of the National AI Service Innovation Task Force. Kim founded and ran a tech startup, MightyWorks, in 2009 before joining Kakao, where he held senior roles in AI-related business and technology initiatives. The ministry said his experience in both AI services and organizational management would help the task force establish itself quickly and deliver services at a faster pace.

The task force, established this year, aims to develop and deliver AI services that address public needs by combining private-sector innovation with public-sector accountability. Unlike the traditional approach of outsourcing development to private contractors, the unit will directly identify public demand, address practical problems and build services in-house. It comprises four teams with a total of 61 members: 26 private-sector developers, 16 AI champions, 13 government officials and six experts from related organizations. The AI champions are practitioners trained and certified under a Ministry of the Interior and Safety program to lead the adoption of AI across government agencies.

Kim's term will run through September 2028. Kim said AI innovation that people can experience firsthand goes beyond introducing new technologies and starts with solving the inconveniences people face in their everyday lives. He said he would draw on his private-sector experience in AI technology and service development to combine the speed and innovation of private companies with public-sector accountability. He said he would deliver AI services that provide tangible benefits to the public as quickly as possible.

The ministry announced in August that it would recruit private-sector developers for the task force, before opening applications for the chief position in September. Kim was appointed following a selection process that included a review of applications and interviews. The task force will begin a new round of recruitment for private-sector developers in early November to strengthen its AI service development capabilities as it begins full-scale operations. Further details, including available positions, eligibility requirements and application timelines, will be announced on the ministry's website.

Articles.Title: Ex-Kakao AI executive named head of public AI services task force

stories.Headline: Incheon Int'l Airport uses AI to predict baggage system failures
stories.Summary:
Incheon International Airport Corp. began using an AI system at Terminal 2 on Oct. 26 to identify baggage-handling equipment at risk of failure. Sensors and machine-learning software monitor sorters, conveyor motors and arrival-hall carousels, flagging potential problems so crews can act before breakdowns. The airport expects preventive maintenance to reduce unexpected shutdowns and repair costs, extend equipment life and help prevent baggage delays. The BHS Smart Monitoring System displays results on a three-level scale: green for normal, yellow for caution and red for danger.

The system also identifies the likely cause of each flagged problem, allowing maintenance crews to replace parts or take other steps before a fault occurs. Previously, maintenance crews mostly repaired equipment after parts had failed. Cho Yong-soo, executive director of operations at Incheon International Airport Corp., said the system is expected to lower baggage-equipment management costs and improve passenger convenience. He added that the airport will continue to speed up the adoption of advanced digital technologies to make operations more stable and keep improving passenger convenience.

The BHS is a network of conveyors and sorting machines that moves checked luggage between check-in counters, aircraft and arrival halls. The system tracks key equipment in real time, including baggage sorters, the motors that drive the conveyors and the baggage carousels in arrival halls. Sensors collect data from the equipment, and machine-learning software analyzes it to find parts that are likely to fail. The airport said the switch to preventive maintenance is expected to prevent unexpected shutdowns, make equipment last longer and lower repair costs. It also expects fewer bags to be delayed, which would make travel easier for passengers.

Articles.Title: Incheon Int'l Airport uses AI to predict baggage system failures

stories.Headline: AI doomsday hype is "stealing all the attention" from immediate threats, Wharton's Mollick says
stories.Summary:
Wharton professor Ethan Mollick said in interviews with Axios and Business Insider, published on November 2, 2026, that the AI industry's focus on existential risk is pulling attention away from more immediate problems. He spoke around the release of his new book, "Co-Existence," which is described as a field guide to AI. He said that while people should worry about the apocalypse, there are about 1,000 other things he is really worried about that are already going to happen. He pointed to AI's effect on jobs as one example.

Mollick said the response should be policy that encourages AI to be used to augment work rather than automate it. He warned that if the panic about AI becomes only about it killing everyone, there will be no room to talk about anything else. He said the same technology that is damaging schools could also serve as a universal tutor, and that it might change health care for the better. He argued that people get to make choices about how the technology works and should focus on the upsides as well as the risks.

Mollick said most CEOs he talks to do not know what to do with the technology, and that pure automation is not what they want either. He said firing all your staff and replacing them with AI is not how you build competitive advantage, and that jobs tend to evolve, which can feel catastrophic or exciting depending on the job. He said he would like to see deep reporting on what is actually happening inside companies, and that worker and manager perspectives rarely come up. He said he uses AI for everything, and that while he writes his own drafts, AI found errors in his writing and in the sources he cited.

In the Business Insider interview, Mollick said advice to learn AI or find an AI-proof career, such as plumbing or nursing, is not very useful. He said that works until something like "PlumBot 6000" comes along, and that robotics experts he knows went from saying large language models were unrelated to robotics to saying there is something there. His book argues that the models are improving much faster than most people understand, and that the only way to deal with their rapid acceleration is to learn to live with them. That means accepting that much of what people can do today will be less useful in the future and focusing on the attributes they have that AI cannot replicate.

Articles.Title: AI doomsday hype is "stealing all the attention" from immediate threats, Wharton's Mollick says

stories.Headline: How Transportation Fleets Deploy AI Today
stories.Summary:
Transportation industry leaders spoke at the WEX OTR Summit in Ponte Vedra, Florida, last week about how fleets are using artificial intelligence in daily work. Patrick Cozzens, president and CEO of Modern Transportation Services, said his team uses AI agents for background analysis during customer negotiations and relies on smart camera systems to improve fleet safety. Ahmad Kakar, CEO and founder of Euclid, said his company provides agents for logistics organizations to automate back-office duties. Shawn Hicklen, chief operating officer of Venture Express, took part in the panel discussion.

The agents handle tasks such as log auditing, driver management, load entry and cash application. An automated agent now handles roughly 85% to 90% of invoice matching, which speeds up billing cycles. About 95% of driver applications are completed on mobile phones rather than computers or tablets, and recruiting agents can call applicants within five minutes to address missing information. The executives said AI shifts employees from mundane data entry to high-judgment, strategic work rather than causing layoffs.

Kakar stressed that system security and containment are vital as deployment accelerates. He cautioned that giving anything unlimited access to everything leads to trouble, and said agents should be built narrowly to follow the cybersecurity principle of least privilege. Cozzens said invoice matching is a task every human hates because it is laborious and delays the billing cycle. Hicklen said the goal is not cutting heads but reallocating hours with existing talent to help the business grow.

Hicklen said drivers really engage with the recruiting agents and appreciate the quick response, almost treating them like a human being. Cozzens said a recruiting agent, even a voice-oriented one, can call back within five minutes of an application being completed and point out what is missing. AI agents can also schedule follow-ups at unconventional hours like 3:00 a.m. when human staff are unavailable. The article does not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: How Transportation Fleets Deploy AI Today

stories.Headline: Trump says he will form new 'AI Force' but continues to call AI fears a 'hoax'
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump said on Saturday, September 19, 2026, that he would move to create a new "AI Force" and promised to appoint an AI czar in the near future. He made the announcement in a post on social media, likening the force to Space Force, which was created during his first term. Trump also continued to call fears about AI alignment a "hoax." It is unclear what the "AI Force" would be tasked with doing, and the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump said the U.S. would form the "AI Force" to look out for the "bad" aspects of AI. He said another armed forces branch would require further action from Congress, and Space Force itself was created by an act of Congress in 2020 as a sixth branch under the Department of Defense. Trump said the U.S. could already handle bad actors "very easily" through the existing criminal and civil justice system. He also said his administration would not hinder or stifle the growth of the industry, and that it would cherish, help and watch over it as it grows.

Trump's comments came after warnings from top tech leaders about the potential dangers of AI. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a blog post last week calling to slow the pace of AI development, and shortly afterward OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said his company would welcome a slower pace so capabilities don't get ahead of alignment and monitoring. Some lawmakers have also called for more guardrails around AI development. Trump responded at the time that the warnings were a "HOAX" and that there was a "SICK conspiracy" going on around AI.

David Sacks, co-chair of Trump's science and technology council, indicated at a Politico conference on Wednesday that more regulations were not necessarily needed. Sacks, who previously served as the White House's former AI and crypto czar until stepping down in March, said the starting point for talking about AI regulation is to realize the regulations that already exist. He said there is a highly regulated administrative state, with many laws and regulations that pertain to AI and many agencies that promulgate them. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Trump's promise to name an AI czar in the near future.

Articles.Title: Trump says he will form new 'AI Force' but continues to call AI fears a 'hoax' - ABC13 Houston

stories.Headline: Heimstaden is changing residential real estate management with AI
stories.Summary:
In June 2025, Heimstaden’s leadership decided to accelerate its use of AI and chose OpenAI after evaluating several platforms. The European residential real estate operator used ChatGPT and Codex to change how it rents out and manages homes. In the Netherlands, the cost of producing a virtually staged property image fell from about €50 to less than €0.10, a reduction of more than 99%. Heimstaden estimates annual savings potential of €130,000 in that market alone.

Heimstaden’s environmental sustainability analyst Julia Erlandsen, who has no software development background, used Codex to help assess environmental risks across the portfolio. Codex supported discovery, cleaning and standardisation of data, quality checking and repeatable processing pipelines, while Erlandsen kept control of methodology and validation. The work assessed 20,112 property assets and generated more than six million rows of useful data. Heimstaden says the estimated delivery requirement fell from five people working for a year to two people working for two months, and it avoided engaging external consultants. After ChatGPT Enterprise launched in September 2025, half of employees were using it within two to three months.

Helge Krogsbøl, Co-CEO, said the purpose of the buildings has not changed, which is providing homes for people, but the way they are operated keeps changing as the company challenges conventions and adopts new technology. Nikolaj Brammer, Chief Digital Officer, described an AI strategy based on three pillars: empowering employees through training and tools, a central transformation office with a network of AI champions, and making property management systems and data models ready for AI. He said letting shows the approach is not about automating one task but improving how the whole process works. Andreas Kalmar Lindquist, Manager of the AI First Team, said people across the business are finding practical ways to use AI, and the job is to scale what works while keeping data secure, responsibilities clear and people in control.

Employees remain responsible for reviewing and approving AI-generated content and decisions. Heimstaden is rolling out a Procurement Intelligence Platform that combines workflow automation with OpenAI models accessed through APIs and works across Outlook, SharePoint and Teams. It is also co-developing Amplio Estate, a property management system designed to support AI-powered workflows through MCP, so employees can retrieve property information and take action in core systems with human oversight. The company describes this as turning the idea of self-operating buildings into a practical technology roadmap.

Articles.Title: Heimstaden is changing residential real estate management with AI

stories.Headline: Before you buy an AI agent, make it pass an exit test
stories.Summary:
Suneet Malhotra, an independent practitioner-researcher, wrote in InfoWorld on November 3, 2026 about moving his own setup from one coding agent to another. The move took about 10 minutes and seemed to go well. The first agent had a global instruction file, 114 skill folders, 189 small memory notes spread across 24 projects and 73 scripts that call its command-line tool. To give a second agent the same footing, he copied the instruction file to the name the other tool reads, AGENTS.md, and ran a find-and-replace on the product name. He did not read the result properly until that month, and the file sat in his home directory for almost three months looking like a finished migration.

The copied file told the new agent to make every model call with Codex -p, where -p is short for -profile, so following it literally would load a configuration profile named after whatever prompt it was handed. The file also still warned the new agent in bold never to use the old vendor's API key. Nothing errored. Malhotra calls this the exit problem in miniature, because the work did not come with the switch and nothing told him. He notes that the EU Data Act's cloud switching rules have applied since September 2025, and that from January 2027 providers cannot charge customers for the switch itself, though those rules were written for data processing services.

Malhotra recommends that buyers run an exit test before signing or renewing, using one realistic maintenance task such as upgrading a logging library across a service with a dozen modules. Partway through, a human decision changes the plan, for example keeping the old log format for one downstream consumer. The first agent should get about halfway, then stop, and the product should export whatever it says represents the work, meaning requirements, decisions, completed actions and remaining steps. That export alone goes to a second agent from a different vendor in a fresh session. The test checks four things: whether finished work is redone, whether a retired assumption comes back, how long a human spends rebuilding context, and what broke on the way over, such as instruction files naming one vendor's commands, skills in one tool's format, hooks tied to one tool's events and credentials scoped to one product.

He advises running the drill twice, once inside the same product and once across vendors, and not letting the vendor pick the task. Buyers should ask vendors to run the drill live on their task using the real export format, ask what the export contains field by field, whether decisions and completed actions are stored separately from the chat log, whether memory and skill formats are documented well enough for another tool to read, and what happens to that state when the contract ends. He says a vendor that trusts its product should be happy to do this, and that a slide about open models and a link to a protocol spec shows the exit story covers the model and not the work. Results should be recorded like a test report and run again at renewal. He adds one caveat in fairness to vendors: some state is genuinely hard to move, and the test is meant to put a number on the cost while the buyer still has leverage.

Articles.Title: Before you buy an AI agent, make it pass an exit test

stories.Headline: Cohere Hits US$25bn as Canada & NVIDIA Fund Sovereign AI
stories.Summary:
Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E funding round targeting up to CAD7bn, or US$5bn, at a valuation of CAD35.7bn, or US$25.5bn, according to a November 2, 2026 article in AI Magazine. The round is the largest private financing round ever undertaken by a Canadian technology company. Backers include the Schwarz Group as lead investor, returning investor NVIDIA, Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital, Inovia Capital, Prosperity7 Ventures and the Government of Canada. Bloomberg had reported the week before that Cohere was raising a large round at a US$20.5bn pre-money valuation.

Canada has committed to an equity investment of up to about CAD1.6bn, or US$1.1bn, to be made in stages. As part of the deal the government says the investment will create at least 1,000 new high-paying Canadian technical jobs by 2030, and Cohere will commit at least CAD1.7bn, or US$1.2bn, to additional computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030. Cohere will keep its Canadian incorporation and headquarters, invest in Canadian research partnerships, create opportunities for students and recent graduates, and keep working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute. Cohere says the money will accelerate frontier enterprise models, full-stack AI products, solutions for regulated industries and long-term compute infrastructure. The company says its customer base grew 20 times over the past year to 300 customers, including Aston Martin Aramco, Bell Canada, Fujitsu, RBC, RWS, PwC, TD Bank and TKMS.

Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said the company was founded in Canada on the belief that the country could build AI companies able to compete at the highest level globally, and that the investment helps attract world-class talent and build secure, sovereign technology from Canada for customers around the world. He said organisations need greater control over their data, infrastructure and how AI is deployed. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada's investment is an investment in choice and security, and that true sovereignty depends on the ability to build, adopt and govern AI on the country's own terms. He said it is in all Canadians' interests for Cohere to succeed and that Canadians will now have a share in that success.

The article frames the round as part of a broader global shift toward sovereign AI, with the US and China currently dominating through firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Moonshot, and challengers emerging in Europe, including Mistral. Cohere has expanded across the UK and Europe, including a combination with Germany's Aleph Alpha and the planned acquisition of Czech cybersecurity company AISLE. The founders said they will use the funds to build what they called a frontier company outside the US and China. The article does not say what happens next beyond the initial close of the round.

Articles.Title: Cohere Hits US$25bn as Canada & NVIDIA Fund Sovereign AI

stories.Headline: Microsoft Q1 FY 2027: Copilot Consumption Expands the AI Business
stories.Summary:
Microsoft reported its Q1 FY 2027 results on November 2, 2026, with revenue of $92.28 billion, up 19% year over year and above the Wall Street consensus of $90.63 billion. Agents and Infra revenue was $76.80 billion, up 25%, while Devices and Consumer revenue was $15.48 billion, down 3%. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion, up 30%, and Azure revenue rose 48%. Operating income was $45.92 billion, up 21%, at a margin of about 50%, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $4.89, up 18%.

Copilot now combines subscription and consumption billing, and daily users rose nearly 50% quarter over quarter and more than fivefold year over year. Customers actively consuming credits through usage-based billing grew more than 75% quarter over quarter, and GitHub agents open more than one-third of pull requests. Foundry passed 120,000 customers, with revenue more than tripling year over year, and Microsoft added 24 data centers across five continents. Fabric exceeded 44,000 paid customers, and the Agent 365 registry passed 50 million agents.

Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and chief executive officer, said the company announced its biggest Copilot update to date, bringing Chat, Cowork, Autopilot and Code into one unified experience. He said it is one product experience across commercial and consumer with all of Office built in, and described Copilot as the new operating system for work. The analyst take said Microsoft's challenge is turning deeper usage into durable customer value while keeping infrastructure availability and sales practices aligned with demand. It also noted weaker sales execution in Microsoft 365 E3 and standalone offerings and an expectation of slower consumption adoption outside coding.

Microsoft guided Q2 FY 2027 revenue to $96 billion to $97.1 billion, or 18% to 19% growth, with Agents and Infra at $80.1 billion to $80.7 billion. It expects Azure growth of 49% to 50% at constant currency and a Microsoft Cloud gross margin of about 65%. Capital expenditures are expected to exceed $50 billion in Q2, and calendar-year 2026 spending of about $170 billion reflects delayed third-party capacity deliveries. The article says the next phase depends on converting expanding AI usage into recurring consumption revenue while improving returns on infrastructure investments.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Q1 FY 2027: Copilot Consumption Expands the AI Business

stories.Headline: Why Anthropic's AI warning is targeting investors | The Global Story
stories.Summary:
Anthropic has issued a warning about artificial intelligence that is aimed at investors, according to a BBC Global Story segment dated 3 November 2026. The warning was covered in a BBC programme that examines why the company is directing its message at people who put money into AI. The same date appears on the BBC listing for the episode. The articles do not give further details of what the warning says.

The articles give no numbers, dates or names beyond the 3 November 2026 date and the company name Anthropic. They do not describe any requirement or change that the warning brings. They also do not say what specific action, if any, investors are being asked to take. No further specifics are provided in the source material.

The articles do not name anyone responsible for the warning or give any statements from Anthropic or its officials. No paraphrased comments from the company appear in the material. The only attribution is to the BBC programme The Global Story. The articles do not say who else, if anyone, was involved.

The context given is limited to the BBC listing, which places the segment among other news items from the same date. The articles do not say what happens next after the warning. They do not describe any response from investors or regulators. No follow-up steps are mentioned in the source material.

stories.Headline: ChatGTP and the Search for Truth: OpenAI Says It Receives 70 Million Religion Requests Weekly
stories.Summary:
OpenAI has said that ChatGPT receives about 70 million religion-related questions every week, according to an analysis reported by The Christian Post and covered by the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association on November 2, 2026. The analysis found that Islam-related questions make up nearly half of all religious questions, while Christianity-related questions make up about one-third. About 22 million of the 70 million questions centered on studying religious texts, and about 16 million pertained to religious holidays and practices. Hinduism was the third most researched religion at 4%, followed by Judaism at 2% and Buddhism at 1%.

The report said religion topics spiked around certain holidays, with Christianity-related questions rising around Easter and Islam-related questions rising around Ramadan and Eid al-Adha. For Christianity-related questions, almost 50% pertained to Bible passages, and about 13% related to worship, sermons or church practices. The researchers said AI is becoming a tool for religious people to support their religious lives and deepen their understanding of their faith. They also said faith leaders are using AI to support their work teaching and organizing those they serve.

The OpenAI researchers said AI should help people pursue what matters to them, including their faith, while strengthening rather than replacing human relationships and institutions. They said AI is not and should not become an arbiter of religious truth or a replacement for spiritual guidance, roles they said belong to individuals, religious leaders and congregations. John Stonestreet, president of the Colson Center for Christian Worldview, told Decision earlier this year that the source of truth is Scripture alone, not artificial intelligence. Clayton Chancey, an enterprise AI architect and founder of Foray Consulting, said the great call is to discernment and warned against offloading or outsourcing discernment to a machine.

Articles.Title: ChatGTP and the Search for Truth: OpenAI Says It Receives 70 Million Religion Requests Weekly

stories.Headline: AMD Falls as Intel PC Warning Dims Meta AI Deal
stories.Summary:
Advanced Micro Devices shares fell to about $477.84 in Monday afternoon trading on November 2, 2026, down $26.96 or 5.34% from the previous close of $504.80. The stock opened at $513.52, hit its intraday high at that same level, and later dropped to $477.69. The decline came ahead of AMD's fiscal third-quarter report, which was scheduled for after the U.S. market close on Tuesday, November 3. Investors were weighing Intel's PC warning against AMD's expanded AI work with Meta Platforms.

Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $0.25 per share in its third-quarter release. Intel CFO David Zinsner said the company sees the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year. AMD competes directly with Intel in x86 PC processors and data center server CPUs, so Intel's warning served as a broader demand signal for chip investors. The options market was pricing an 8.95% move, or about $45.17 per share, in either direction around AMD's earnings report.

AMD recently unveiled a deepened strategic partnership with Meta Platforms that calls for AMD to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering and deploy Helios rack-scale AI computing systems at Meta data centers. Initial Helios systems have been installed and are undergoing testing ahead of a broader rollout, and Meta has already deployed millions of AMD EPYC processors across multiple generations. The deal sits alongside Meta's plan to raise up to $95 billion for AI infrastructure expansion. Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis reiterated a Buy rating on AMD and maintained a $650 price target, expecting third-quarter revenue of $13.5 billion and fourth-quarter revenue of $17 billion, above the $16.3 billion consensus estimate.

Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland also reiterated a Buy rating and expects AMD's data center GPU revenue to reach about $41 billion in 2027. He raised his 2027 server CPU revenue estimate to $33 billion from $30 billion, with a total data center revenue forecast of $74 billion, above the $71 billion consensus estimate. AMD is trading near its session low with earnings due after Tuesday's close. Market watchers are weighing PC-demand concerns against AMD's AI infrastructure partnership with Meta and analysts' data center revenue forecasts.

Articles.Title: AMD Falls as Intel PC Warning Dims Meta AI Deal

stories.Headline: Anthropic Builds World's Tiniest Dam Against AI Clone Game Flood
stories.Summary:
Anthropic recently added new rules to the guidelines that govern Claude, its AI assistant, according to a report by Game Developer cited by Aftermath. A Claude user noticed the update in the last few days, and Anthropic confirmed the change. The new rules say Claude should build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. They also say Claude should not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.

Anthropic employee Addy Osmani said in a tweet that the sentences were added to steer Claude away from recreating someone else's specific game, because using Claude to infringe intellectual property is against the company's usage policy. He said original games, genre games, and games built from users' own designs and assets are meant to keep working. Eurogamer reported that some users ran into problems with the new rules during what they felt was legitimate use. One said they make personalized digital modules of board wargames under paid commission for clients, from games the clients own, and another had trouble making a single-player version of a board game for internal study. A user on the Claude subreddit said Claude refused to tweak a single-player version of Carcassonne it had made for them.

Aftermath reported that the change is unlikely to do much to stop AI clones of games, because people can use other tools if Claude refuses, and because the programs are easy to trick with workarounds. The article said users do not have to ask directly for a specific game, and gave the example of asking for a game about an Italian plumber with a mustache who travels through pipes. It also said the discourse on the Claude subreddit was divided, with some people saying it is good that Anthropic will stop people from stealing, others noting the whole thing is built on theft, and still others seeing it as the games industry clamping down because companies got afraid they would lose revenue. The article said it is unlikely there will be any meaningful change.

Articles.Title: Anthropic Builds World's Tiniest Dam Against AI Clone Game Flood

stories.Headline: Proton’s CEO Cancels AI ‘Re-Interviews’
stories.Summary:
Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide re-interviews on Friday, according to six current employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media. The re-interviews would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership. The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday into how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton. That investigation showed Yen pushing AI in some cases despite security concerns from employees.

The investigation was based on conversations with eight current and one former Proton employees, Slack chats, meeting audio, and an AI manifesto written by the company’s CTO Bart Butler. In one exchange at the end of August, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. Yen replied that this was “bullshit and loser thinking,” said it was of course possible to be fast and secure, and told employees to stop thinking always of how to be slower and focus more on how to be faster. He added that they should stop lovingly handcrafting all their code and use AI more.

The investigation painted a picture of Proton that is very different to the public’s perception of a company carefully protecting privacy, and found that Proton is barreling ahead with AI in large part to achieve more annual revenue. It also found a culture of fear across Proton, where employees have genuine concerns about security or being asked to develop security-focused products with AI, but feel unable to voice them because Yen mocks or insults employees in front of everyone else. After the all-hands meeting on Friday, one employee told 404 Media that they did not think Yen would change anything, and that the only reason the meeting happened was because he has a rebellion on his hands. The re-interview cancellations likely do not address the concerns of many Proton users, who are more focused on Proton’s deprioritization of security, and many have blasted the company’s leadership on social media over the last 24 hours and explicitly called for Yen to resign.

Articles.Title: Proton’s CEO Cancels AI ‘Re-Interviews’

stories.Headline: Meta Rolls Out AI Business Assistant To All Advertisers, Agencies 04/24/2026
stories.Summary:
Meta has begun rolling out the beta version of its AI business assistant to advertisers and agencies of all sizes across major global markets and languages, according to an announcement from the company this week. The tool first launched with small businesses in the U.S. last October. Meta says businesses using the automated assistant resolved common account issues at a 20% higher rate. They also saw a 12% decrease in ad cost per result after applying the assistant's opportunity score recommendations.

The assistant is designed to improve campaign performance through tailored AI-powered recommendations and real-time guidance based on an account's business data. It can also quickly restore disabled accounts, update spend limits, and troubleshoot payment or delivery errors. Advertisers and agency partners can reach it within Ads Manager, Meta Business Suite, and Business Support Home. Meta said it will keep iterating the assistant based on advertiser feedback, and that expanded capabilities focused on campaign planning and creation are expected throughout 2026.

Meta described the assistant as part of its broader AI push, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg saying on the company's Q4 investor call that AI is starting to understand users' personal context, including their history, interests, content and relationships. He said much of what makes agents valuable is the unique context they can see. The expansion comes as Meta cuts its employee base while investing heavily in AI chips, top AI talent, data centers and AI acquisitions, including the purchase of the AI agent and social-media platform Moltbook. Meta's earlier chatbots on Instagram drew criticism after being flagged for flirting and romantic role play with underage users and for generating racist and violent remarks, and after The Washington Post reported that the chatbots gave teen accounts information about how to commit suicide. Meta then said teens would no longer be able to access AI characters until an updated experience is ready.

Articles.Title: Meta Rolls Out AI Business Assistant To All Advertisers, Agencies 04/24/2026

stories.Headline: Microsoft's Satya Nadella envisions AI agents replacing traditional apps
stories.Summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced a shift away from traditional operating systems and applications toward AI agents that can carry out tasks across platforms. He spoke at the Build 2026 developer conference, according to a TechGig report updated on June 03, 2026. Nadella said users will increasingly rely on intelligent agents that handle tasks seamlessly across various platforms, without navigating multiple applications. He likened the change to earlier shifts from mainframe computers to personal computing and smartphones.

The approach centers on what Microsoft calls agent-first computing and on Project Solara, a new chip-to-cloud platform developed with Qualcomm. The platform is meant to support AI systems that work across devices and workflows without traditional app-based interactions. Microsoft described a phased transition, starting with AI working alongside existing applications, then moving to deeper integration, and finally reaching a state where AI agents operate independently of applications. The company said AI agents could redefine software use, with less focus on standalone applications and more on autonomous systems that interpret user intent and act on it. Microsoft also said users may interact with technology mainly through natural language prompts, with agents managing tasks such as scheduling and data analysis.

Nadella said AI systems will serve as the primary interface between users and technology, moving beyond mere assistants inside applications. He described the shift as a significant transformation in computing toward an era of agents. Microsoft said the change could pose challenges for developers and software companies, because the traditional dominance of standalone applications and software layers may diminish in favor of more integrated AI-driven solutions. The report did not say what happens next beyond the phased approach Microsoft outlined.

Articles.Title: microsofts satya nadella envisions ai agents replacing traditional apps

stories.Headline: The rules of getting ahead are changing in the AI era. Not everyone stands to benefit
stories.Summary:
Microsoft chief economic opportunity officer Aneesh Raman has been predicting the death of the traditional career ladder as AI reshapes the workplace. He spoke at Aspen Digital's WIN Summit in late October, where Fortune's Kristin Stoller asked him about the implications for women and other historically marginalized groups. Raman envisions a "climbing wall" in place of the ladder, where progress isn't always upward and workers chart their own paths based on their skills, interests and opportunities. He acknowledged that losing the familiar career playbook could initially be intimidating.

Raman argued the change could ultimately give workers more freedom to advance in ways that suit their strengths and ambitions. He said that over time people start to climb in ways unique to them. Part of the answer, he said, is "radical transparency," meaning workers should understand how AI is changing their jobs and what opportunities they have to shape their own careers. He also believes women could have an edge in the AI era because they over-index on human skills such as empathy and judgement. He predicts more women will become CEOs and that women's representation on corporate boards could climb from roughly a third to half or more.

New research from Nicole Smith, a senior researcher at Pew Research Center, found that in more AI-exposed occupations, men's employment grew 6.3% for each one-point increase in an occupation's exposure score, while women's barely changed. Among workers with a high school diploma or less, women's employment fell. Smith said men are much more optimistic about AI than women and may be more inclined to use it to pursue new opportunities. She said the conversation needs to change and be opened to women. The question now, according to the article, is whether employers can make career advancement more flexible without making the path to success less equitable.

Articles.Title: The rules of getting ahead are changing in the AI era. Not everyone stands to benefit

stories.Headline: OpenAI doubles Pro limits, integrates Work features into ChatGPT
stories.Summary:
OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Work capabilities directly into its regular Chat interface, according to an email seen by BleepingComputer. The company is also combining usage allowances across its ChatGPT and Codex subscriptions. The changes were reported on November 3, 2026. The combined experience will first be tested with a small group of users in the coming weeks.

Users selected for the test will be able to bring in their files and plugins. This will let them ask ChatGPT to build websites, create presentations, or perform web-based tasks while reviewing its progress. ChatGPT and Codex will now draw from a single allowance, though Unlimited Instant usage will not count toward that shared limit. More advanced models and complex tasks will use a greater portion of the allowance, and users can check their remaining usage and reset times under Settings and Usage.

OpenAI had already doubled Work and Codex allowances for its Pro 100, Pro 200, and Pro 500 subscriptions, effective October 29. OpenAI said the aim is to let users move between exploring ideas and completing complex tasks without switching modes. The company described the test as limited to a small group of users in the coming weeks. It said selected users will be able to incorporate their files and plugins.

OpenAI also clarified that Unlimited Instant usage will not count against the shared allowance. The report gives no further details on timing beyond the coming weeks or on which users will be chosen for the test. It does not say when the combined experience might reach all users. It also does not say how the shared allowance will be measured beyond noting that complex tasks use more of it.

Articles.Title: OpenAI doubles Pro limits, integrates Work features into ChatGPT

stories.Headline: Microsoft's AI Risk Report Misses This Key Detail
stories.Summary:
Microsoft released its 2026 Digital Defense Report, and Andrew Grotto, a Stanford University director, wrote in Dark Reading on November 2, 2026, that the report misses a key detail. The report assessed that government agencies and services were the most affected by cyber threats and were frequently targeted for nation-state activity. Grotto wrote that the report has a major blind spot: the impact of legacy software, especially Microsoft's own, on organizations' cyber-risk. He noted that Microsoft deserves some credit for using AI to evaluate products it has already deployed.

Grotto wrote that Microsoft holds an 85% market share in the US public sector productivity software market. According to CISA, Microsoft accounts for nearly 16% of known exploited vulnerabilities so far this year, the most of any company, and nearly 23% from November 2021 to October 2026. The next-highest vendor, Cisco, is responsible for approximately 7% in 2026 and 6% total. Grotto also cited Microsoft's record-setting Patch Tuesday count of 974 vulnerabilities disclosed last month.

Grotto wrote that US government officials and advisory bodies have concluded that breaches by Chinese and Russian state-sponsored actors were preventable and caused by Microsoft's negligence. He wrote that all software vendors, including Microsoft, should invest more in security before products are released, even at the expense of slowing new features. He added that vendors should be transparent with customers about these processes so customers can make more informed purchasing decisions. He warned that otherwise the 2027 report will paint an even darker picture.

Grotto wrote that attackers are already using AI to generate novel attacks and orchestrate complex, large-scale campaigns. He wrote that AI is enabling criminal groups to achieve successes normally reserved for nation-state actors, and that nation-state actors are using AI to increase the scale and sophistication of their operations. He described the threat level as rising at an alarming rate. He wrote that legacy software will remain the substrate of organizations' attack surface for the foreseeable future.

Articles.Title: Microsoft's AI Risk Report Misses This Key Detail

stories.Headline: OpenAI and King’s examine teen AI safety and youth voice
stories.Summary:
OpenAI and King’s College London held a workshop in London to examine how generative AI affects young people’s learning, wellbeing and development. The event brought together researchers, educators, clinicians, policymakers and youth organizations, according to an article published on 3 November 2026 by EdTech Innovation Hub. Participants questioned whether a single approach to youth safety could serve users with different developmental needs, family circumstances and access to support. They also looked at tensions between parental oversight and teenagers’ rights to privacy and growing independence.

The workshop drew on OpenAI’s European Youth Safety Blueprint, which proposes age-appropriate experiences, privacy-preserving age assurance, protections against manipulative outputs and parental controls. Participants said a 13-year-old and a 17-year-old need different protections, and that confidence in using a chatbot does not mean a young person can judge its answers. The discussion was supported by the King’s Institute for Artificial Intelligence. Organizations represented included UNICEF Innocenti, European Schoolnet, Parent Zone, Kooth UK, the University of Oxford and University College London.

Dr Nessa Keddo, Senior Lecturer in Media, Diversity and Technology at King’s College London, said youth experiences with AI are not linear as tools and features expand quickly. She said research should look at differences between geographic locations, protected characteristic groups and people from multiple disadvantaged backgrounds, and that young people should be co-designers and participants in future research. Rafaela Nicolazzi, EMEA Privacy and Consumers Protection Lead for Global Affairs at OpenAI, said the blueprint is grounded in a commitment to treat teens as teens. She said there is no one-size-fits-all approach and that responsible design must be informed by different ages, contexts and lived experiences.

The workshop called for young people to influence research, evaluation, product development and governance, with chances to shape decisions beyond being consulted. OpenAI representatives discussed learning-focused features for teenagers, parental controls and safeguards for high-risk conversations. OpenAI’s AI and Teen Development Research Grant program will support independent studies of how AI affects 13- to 17-year-olds. King’s and OpenAI are also exploring further activity through the Wellbeing Council on AI and other opportunities for collaboration.

Articles.Title: OpenAI and King’s examine teen AI safety and youth voice | ETIH EdTech News

stories.Headline: Anthropic may soon reach the AI self-improvement threshold — TechCrunch
stories.Summary:
Anthropic said in an updated S-1/A filing that it may soon reach its own threshold of sharply accelerated AI-driven progress, according to TechCrunch. The company said this concerns its internal assessment of future models rather than its current systems. The filing was reported on 2 November 2026, and UA.NEWS published its account on 3 November 2026. Anthropic said it uses artificial intelligence systems to speed up research and development.

Anthropic warned that this could speed up model development faster than it can develop, test and put in place appropriate safety, alignment and security measures. The company also acknowledged that in the past it did not always immediately identify significant acceleration in the pace of model development. It said it may fail to recognize such acceleration in time in the future. Anthropic stressed that none of its current models has yet been identified as having exceeded this threshold, and it said data evaluation is ongoing.

The process in which AI helps train and improve later systems so effectively that it sharply accelerates the development of its capabilities is called recursive self-improvement, or RSI. Anthropic considers the use of AI to create more powerful models both an opportunity and a significant safety risk. The company said it currently does not expect to be able to safely use Claude for fully autonomous design and creation of the next generations of frontier models without meaningful human oversight or understanding of the process. Anthropic is considering updating its Responsible Scaling Policy to preserve human control over the development of frontier models.

Articles.Title: Anthropic may soon reach the AI self-improvement threshold — TechCrunch

stories.Headline: WeChange.AI helps save public sector staff 2-5 hours per week with Microsoft Azure services
stories.Summary:
WeChange.AI, a company founded in the United Kingdom in 2024, built a platform called Navigator on Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Fabric and Power BI to help public sector organizations understand how employees actually use technology. The company was started by Andrew Boxall, who spent a decade on technology adoption in the public sector and later worked on Microsoft's public sector team. Navigator asks individuals to reflect on their day-to-day digital experience and matches their answers to personalized recommendations, resources and learning. At the organizational level, those responses roll up into Power BI dashboards that give leaders an aggregated view of adoption gaps and accessibility needs. WeChange.AI now works with more than 50 public sector organizations, with more than 70 others actively procuring or onboarding, including two national government customers.

The platform is approaching 80,000 Navigator submissions, with around 24,000 people sharing a disability, neurodivergence or similar accessibility need. More than 22,000 people identified at least one specific requirement they want support with, and Navigator now connects people with more than 160 accessibility resources. Microsoft Fabric, including OneLake and Lakehouse capabilities, became the company's data layer in July 2025, feeding the Power BI reporting customers rely on. Navigator's recommendation engine is intentionally rules-based rather than generative, so WeChange.AI can explain exactly why a recommendation was made, a requirement for customers who must justify systems to regulators, auditors and the public. Customers report saving between two and five hours per person, per week by making better use of Microsoft tools they already owned.

Boxall said the company made a deliberate decision to build on Azure and the wider Microsoft ecosystem because it needed a platform that could scale alongside its ambitions. He said using Azure Pipelines and a structured approach across development, UAT and production environments let the company move new capabilities into customers' hands faster and with greater confidence. He said he spends less time worrying about deployment, infrastructure and operational complexity and more time solving customer problems. He said the impact he is most proud of is not the platform, the architecture or the AI, but the fact that the technology helps people believe they can do things they did not think were possible before. Darren Kidson, Service Director Digital Data & Technology and CIO at Colchester City Council, said the council had already invested heavily in Microsoft 365 and other digital platforms, but the real challenge was helping people build confidence and skills.

Kidson said Navigator's data revealed lower digital confidence and more resistance among mobile and digital workers than in office-based services, so the council focused on engagement, communications, change champions and targeted training. He said managers could move from assumptions to evidence and see where confidence was high, where barriers existed and where support would have the greatest impact. Izzy Pochin, Resources and Accessibility Lead at WeChange.AI, said accessibility is not synonymous with disability or just compliance, and that it helps everyone participate confidently. WeChange.AI's next ambition is to turn individual organizations' evidence into shared, sector-wide learning through a significant expansion of its benchmarking service, sharing and re-use. Paul Ford, Education Lead at WeChange.AI, pointed to a strong network effect among public sector bodies that face many of the same pressures and stand to gain from shared examples rather than solving the same problems in isolation.

Articles.Title: WeChange.AI helps save public sector staff 2-5 hours per week with Microsoft Azure services

stories.Headline: Naria Santa Lucia leaves Microsoft after seven years leading digital and AI skills initiatives
stories.Summary:
Naria Santa Lucia announced on LinkedIn that she has left Microsoft after seven years, most recently as General Manager of Microsoft Elevate. In that role she led global work on digital skills, AI training and workforce development. She said the initiatives she worked on helped more than 100 million people in around 21 or more countries develop digital and AI skills. She also pointed to the Global Skills Initiative, which was developed and launched during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Santa Lucia joined Microsoft in July 2019 as Senior Director of Skills for Employability. In September 2020 she became General Manager of Digital Inclusion and Community Engagement at Microsoft Philanthropies, and in July 2024 she moved to General Manager at Microsoft Elevate, formerly Microsoft Philanthropies. Her responsibilities covered the company's strategy, investments, programs and partnerships to widen access to digital and AI skills. She worked with governments, educational institutions, businesses and civil society organizations, and with nonprofit partners delivering training and community programs.

In her LinkedIn post she thanked colleagues, the wider Microsoft Elevate Skills team, Microsoft President Brad Smith, former manager Kate Behncken and Microsoft Elevate leader Justin Spelhaug. She wrote that after seven incredible years she had decided to leave Microsoft for her next professional adventure. She has not announced a new employer or formal appointment. She says she intends to keep working with nonprofit organizations and communities through teaching and advisory activities, and that further details will follow.

Before Microsoft, Santa Lucia was Executive Director of the Washington State Opportunity Scholarship from 2014 to 2019. The public-private partnership raised more than $200 million for scholarships and student services, with a goal of supporting more than 20,000 students by 2025, focusing on students from low- and middle-income backgrounds. Her earlier roles included Executive Director of the James B. Moran Center for Youth Advocacy and fundraising leadership at the Legal Foundation of Washington. She has also co-chaired the World Bank's Solutions for Youth Employment initiative and served on the board of Seattle Arts and Lectures, and she is a graduate of the University of Chicago's College and Law School.

Articles.Title: Naria Santa Lucia leaves Microsoft after seven years leading digital and AI skills initiatives

stories.Headline: Support New AI Frameworks Faster Using NVIDIA Workload Map
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA published a technical blog post on November 2, 2026, by Alon Lavian, Yuval Grauer and Ron Lev describing a project called NVIDIA Workload Map. The project provides a common Kubernetes workload description so that schedulers, controllers and platforms can interpret distributed workloads without framework-specific parsing code. It ships with a catalog of prebuilt definitions for frameworks including JobSet, PyTorchJob, RayCluster, RayJob, RayService, KServe, Knative, MPIJob, NVIDIA NIM, LeaderWorkerSet, Milvus, Grove PodCliqueSet and NVIDIA Dynamo. Workload Map is part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform.

The tool ships as a Kubernetes CRD plus a Go library that interprets workload definitions, and the CRD's resource kind remains Karta. Each definition specifies where to find pod templates, replica counts and status fields for its workload type. In the blog's example, a JobSet with one leader and two workers, each requesting four GPUs, totals 12 GPUs, and the Workload Map CLI shows the leader and worker roles and that total. The same JobSet definition supports workload inspection through the CLI, gang scheduling via KAI Scheduler and unified management in NVIDIA Run:ai. Additional workload types can be added by writing a YAML definition.

The blog says the NVIDIA Run:ai team faced the same adapter challenge while building its platform, answering the same questions in code for each new custom resource definition. It says each new framework a customer brings requires another adapter, which is why support for a new workload type often waits for a release. Elotl's Nova uses Workload Map to interpret workload structure and resource requirements for multi-cluster scheduling decisions. The post was written by Alon Lavian, Yuval Grauer and Ron Lev, and NVIDIA notes the content is AI-generated and may summarize information incompletely.

The blog describes Workload Map as part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, which brings together technologies to help the ecosystem design, build and operate more efficient AI factories. It says the platform includes open source, modular software components built to support multi-tenant operations and scaling. For next steps, the blog suggests exploring the workload catalog to find a definition for a framework already in use. It also suggests joining the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack workspace to discuss workload definitions and integrations.

Articles.Title: Support New AI Frameworks Faster Using NVIDIA Workload Map | NVIDIA Technical Blog

stories.Headline: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA published a technical blog on November 2, 2026, describing work by Mark Chmarny and Yuan Chen to make Kubernetes ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 compute trays. The team used the NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime, or AICR, which captures tuned configurations as reusable recipes, generates deployment bundles and validates running clusters. They validated the setup on Vera Rubin NVL72 reference clusters using GPU Operator v26.7.0 and DRA driver v0.5.0. A cross-node NCCL all-reduce test reached 744.71 GB/s bus bandwidth at 16 GiB over the NVLink fabric.

The Vera Rubin recipe family encodes several specific choices, including the host-managed R615.23 open-kernel-module driver and DRA driver v0.5.0 with ComputeDomains. It also specifies Ubuntu 26.04 with a 64k-page kernel, Kubernetes 1.34.1 or later, and platform settings such as higher memory limits for the NFD topology updater. The recipe ships as Preview and covers training, inference and Dynamo inference variants. Compared with GB200 NVL72, Vera Rubin replaces ConnectX-7 NICs and BlueField-3 DPUs with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and BlueField-4 DPUs, and the validated image ships DOCA-OFED 3.3.0.

Running validation on early silicon surfaced an unmapped Rubin architecture value in go-nvlib that crash-looped the DRA driver kubelet plugin. The fix spread through the stack and shipped in the official DRA driver v0.5.0 release, the authors said. They also noted that early validation rounds were briefly blocked by a hardware or fabric issue in one early cluster, which kept one compute tray out of the NVLink fabric. After the hardware was reseated, all GPUs on both nodes joined a single clean fabric clique.

The blog says a first deployment targeted a combination of arm64, Ubuntu 26.04, a 64k-page kernel, RKE2 and Vera Rubin that had never been validated together, and it went from cluster handoff to a healthy runtime in hours. A second Vera Rubin cluster reproduced the result the following day. The authors present the recipe as an early-adopter path that does not yet carry the production support and lifecycle qualification of a Supported recipe. They suggest generating the training or inference recipe with a single command to begin evaluating the validated configuration.

Articles.Title: Making Kubernetes AI-Ready for NVIDIA Vera Rubin on Day One | NVIDIA Technical Blog

stories.Headline: Meta (META) Draws Fresh Heat As AI Spending Bites And Lobbying Team Grows
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms is under pressure after record spending on AI infrastructure pushed its free cash flow negative for the first time since 2012, according to a Simply Wall St article published on November 2, 2026. S&P has shifted Meta's credit outlook to negative, citing concerns about long term capital commitments tied to AI projects. The company is also assembling a bipartisan lobbying team in Washington to influence emerging AI policy ahead of upcoming U.S. elections. The article says these developments should not be viewed in isolation when assessing the stock.

The article says Meta's 2026 capital expenditure is guided at US$130 billion to US$145 billion, alongside large multi-year compute commitments. It also mentions a US$95 billion equity program. The article states that the main thing that has to go right is for Meta to turn this very high AI infrastructure spending into durable earnings power that more than offsets legal, regulatory and youth-safety cost pressures. It adds that the full story points toward a US$848 fair value for Meta Platforms.

The article attributes the negative free cash flow and the credit outlook change to Meta's capital intensity, which it says is no longer an abstract line in guidance but is running through the cash flow statement and S&P's outlook. It says this pressure directly tests analyst concerns about weaker free cash generation if AI products and services do not scale profitably. The article also says the market reaction can be read as investors temporarily downplaying the revenue and engagement gains that analysts already link to Meta's AI ad tools and business messaging. It notes that peers such as Alphabet and Amazon are also racing to fund AI.

The article says Meta Platforms runs social networks, VR devices and AI wearables at global scale, so its record AI infrastructure commitments touch everything from news feeds to hardware. It says that reach helps explain why credit markets, regulators and policymakers all watch its spending choices closely. The article frames the sell-off and credit outlook downgrade as a probe of whether Meta's central bet on very high AI and data center spending still holds when free cash flow briefly turns negative. It does not say what happens next beyond describing the catalysts as ones to watch.

Articles.Title: Meta (META) Draws Fresh Heat As AI Spending Bites And Lobbying Team Grows

stories.Headline: Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) Delivers Strong Azure Growth as AI Demand Exceeds Supply
stories.Summary:
Microsoft reported its results in late October 2026, and the figures were described in Janus Henderson's third-quarter 2026 investor letter. Revenue rose 18% to $90 billion. Azure growth came in at 43%, up from 39%, and management forecast around 45%. Copilot adoption reached 30 million seats after 10 million were added during the quarter.

The letter said management committed to remaining free cash flow positive through fiscal 2027. It also said demand for Azure continues to exceed supply, and that efficiency gains are increasing output from each unit of capacity. Microsoft stock closed at about $521.19 per share on October 29, 2026, with a market capitalization of about $3.82 trillion. Its one-month return was -2.21%, and its shares traded between $349.20 and $551.15 over the last 52 weeks.

Janus Henderson, which runs the Global Sustainable Equity Fund, wrote the letter. The fund returned 1.86% in the third quarter of 2026, matching its benchmark and beating the IA Global peer group's 0.38% return. The managers said they continued to adjust the portfolio around their view that AI adoption will create opportunities for companies with durable competitive advantages, proprietary data, network effects and resilient business models. They also highlighted growing electricity demand from data centres and the potential for renewable energy and battery investments to support energy security and decarbonisation.

The fund's exposure to infrastructure-related companies and its lack of energy holdings weighed on relative performance, partly offset by gains from selected technology, healthcare and financial investments. The managers also noted the risks a strong El Niño could pose to agriculture and inflation. Looking ahead, the fund said it remains focused on balancing AI-related growth opportunities with sustainability considerations, favouring companies with pricing power, resilient operations and long-term structural growth potential amid geopolitical uncertainty, elevated energy prices and higher interest rates. The letter said Microsoft benefits from network effects and an embedded ecosystem across productivity, cloud and developer platforms, which reinforces its competitive moat.

stories.Headline: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA published an open-source tool called NVIDIA Attribution on November 2, 2026, according to a technical blog post by Gargi Prasad, Jason Sewall, Aaron Blakeman, Ajay Hotchandani and Ashwin Poojary. The tool correlates workload-scoped logs, metrics, telemetry and scheduler state to produce a structured diagnosis. That diagnosis includes the outcome, root cause, affected nodes, supporting symptoms and an evidence trail. The post says the system has been used in production across NVIDIA AI infrastructure for years, analyzing millions of workloads each week across hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

The system has two deployable components, the Attribution Service and the Attribution Blueprint. The Service exposes a REST API for the core attribution engine, and the Blueprint is a Python reference orchestrator that connects cluster schedulers and telemetry sources to the Service. The Blueprint ships with execution-context connectors for Slurm, Kueue and static inputs, plus log and metric connectors for Loki, local files, Kubernetes pod logs and PromQL metrics. The attribution process has four stages: scoping the workload, collecting observations, extracting and correlating events through deterministic rules, and returning a structured result with terminal state and attributed domain. In one large RDMA-backed cluster, the tool correlated port errors, connection resets and scheduler events to find patterns around specific host and switch ports.

The post says the quality of attribution depends on the quality and completeness of the underlying telemetry. When multiple causes fit the evidence, the sub_domain is marked ambiguous, so the diagnosis records uncertainty instead of turning incomplete evidence into a definitive diagnosis. A worked example shows an NVLink signal integrity issue on node-02 identified as the root cause while NCCL errors across ranks are kept as supporting symptoms. The post says teams can add rules for new failure modes and connectors for their own schedulers and telemetry backends. It also says downstream systems can consume terminal_state and sub_domain instead of parsing product-specific logs.

The post describes the tool as a complement to readiness checks, continuous health monitoring, and the systems that repair infrastructure and restart workloads. It says the Blueprint can run near each cluster's data sources, with either a dedicated Service for each Blueprint or a shared Service for multiple Blueprints. For next steps, the post tells readers to clone the NVIDIA Attribution repository, follow the quickstart to run the sample workflow and inspect diagnoses in the local dashboard, and review the Blueprint configuration reference to connect their own scheduler and telemetry backends. The quickstart builds the Service and dashboard in Docker and requires Docker and the uv package manager.

Articles.Title: Diagnose Distributed AI Workload Failures with NVIDIA Attribution

stories.Headline: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
stories.Summary:
Anthropic said in a revised S-1A filing on Monday, November 2, 2026, that it may be close to reaching recursive self-improvement, or RSI, the point where AI becomes good enough at training itself to sharply speed up its own capabilities. The filing was reported by TechCrunch, which said the warning appeared in the fine print while attention focused on the company's updated financials, with revenue soaring and expenses rising too. Anthropic added new statements to its Risk Factors section saying it has already used AI to develop new models whose leaps in capability it did not recognize at the time. It also said its internal estimates and expectations for future models, rather than its current models, indicate it may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of "dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI."

The filing says Anthropic has not designated any of its current models as exceeding that threshold and that it continues to assess the underlying data. It says the company uses AI in its research and development but cautions that using AI to help build more capable AI could pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress. Anthropic says this is one of the areas covered by its Responsible Scaling Policy, which sets out plans to monitor and mitigate risks as it approaches what has been termed RSI. The filing also says Anthropic does not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding, if and when that becomes technically possible.

Anthropic said it is considering updates to its Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control of frontier model development. The filing states that its increasing use of AI systems to accelerate its own research and development may cause model capabilities to advance faster than its ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures. As a result, it says it has in the past not identified, and may in the future not identify, a significant acceleration in its rate of development until after it has occurred. TechCrunch noted that skeptics might point out an S-1 functions as both disclosure and marketing, and that claims of being close to a model powerful enough to build itself could fall into the latter category.

TechCrunch said that when the term RSI became popular earlier this year, many believed it was a buzzword or at best a goal too hard to achieve, define, or prove. It also said there is no question that Claude's capabilities, especially in coding, math, and cybersecurity, have grown in leaps and bounds this year. The article said that if Anthropic thinks the possibility of RSI is close, maybe we should believe it and act, perhaps govern, accordingly. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Anthropic's stated plans to consider policy updates and continue assessing the data.

Articles.Title: Anthropic warns that it’s very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI

stories.Headline: AI glasses for sailing: Find a durable pair with useful features
stories.Summary:
Meta published a guide on November 2, 2026, about choosing AI glasses for sailing. The article describes how the glasses offer hands-free access to a camera, open-ear speakers and voice commands through Meta AI. It says users can ask for a weather update, make calls and send messages without reaching for a phone. The piece highlights the Oakley Meta Vanguard as a strong option for sailing.

The Vanguard has a 12 MP camera with a 122-degree field of view and can record video in up to 3K resolution. It uses a five-microphone array, and its speakers are designed to keep sound clear in winds up to 30 mph. The glasses carry an IP67 rating, which under test conditions means they can withstand immersion in up to one meter of fresh water for up to 30 minutes. They offer up to nine hours of use on a full charge, and the included charging case provides up to 36 additional hours. A full charge takes 75 minutes.

The article says all other Meta AI Glasses carry an IPX4 rating, which protects against splashes and light rain but not submersion. It notes that the Vanguard does not currently support prescription lenses, while the Oakley Meta HSTN can accommodate prescriptions from -12 to +6. It also says the glasses pair with a phone over Bluetooth and depend on the phone's connected services. The article advises users not to treat the glasses as a replacement for normal communication and safety equipment on board.

Articles.Title: AI glasses for sailing: Find a durable pair with useful features

stories.Headline: Garland County Library board approves AI policy, change order for new branch - Hot Springs Sentinel Record
stories.Summary:
The Garland County Library Board of Trustees voted on Monday afternoon to establish an artificial intelligence policy for library employees, the Hot Springs Sentinel Record reported. The board also approved a change order for the new North Garland County branch during the same meeting. Executive Director Adam Webb discussed a pair of change orders for the branch at the meeting. The vote came amid the rise of artificial intelligence.

The policy does not require employees to use AI, but it sets guidelines for employees who might use it as part of their workflow. The article gives no further numbers, dates or names beyond the Monday meeting, Webb and the branch. The report was published on Nov. 3, 2026, by James Leigh. The meeting took place Monday afternoon.

Webb discussed the change orders for the new North Garland County branch during the trustees meeting. The article does not say what the change orders involve or what they change about the branch project. It also does not give the vote count or say who else spoke. The reporting is subscriber-exclusive coverage from the Sentinel-Record.

stories.Headline: NeuroDX unveils Sphota AI model, claims 50x data efficiency
stories.Summary:
NeuroDX, an Indian startup backed by the IndiaAI Mission, introduced a 240-million-parameter language model called Sphota. The company announced the model on November 3, 2026. CEO Siddharth Panwar said Sphota scored 52.4 per cent across 11 benchmarks, against 52.1 per cent for a comparable Liquid AI model. The company says the results are preliminary and await independent public evaluations.

According to the company, Sphota used 50 times less training data than the Liquid AI model. It also offers 4.5 times better memory efficiency for conversational context. The architecture grew out of brain research and aims to capture meaning directly instead of relying on next-word prediction. NeuroDX is rebranding as Manaas AI and shifting its focus from healthcare to becoming a foundation model company. A larger model of between 1 billion and 2 billion parameters is being developed, with a December release targeted.

Panwar said Manaas AI was allocated 368 H200 GPUs for 18 months and 12.5 crore rupees under the IndiaAI Mission. That allocation is for developing a 20-billion-parameter multimodal electroencephalogram model. He argued that India should keep developing frontier AI models despite limited computing resources, saying domestic work helps researchers understand advanced AI and build safeguards. Manaas AI plans to keep Sphota's architecture proprietary for now, while IndiaAI Mission-supported models will be open source.

Articles.Title: NeuroDX unveils Sphota AI model, claims 50x data efficiency

stories.Headline: Cybersecurity M&A sees 37 deals in October, AI security expands
stories.Summary:
SecurityWeek reported 37 cybersecurity merger and acquisition deals in October 2026, according to TechGig. The activity included several acquisitions focused on AI-powered security and firmware protection. Absolute Security acquired FirmGuard, the UEFI BIOS firmware security and management business of Phoenix Technologies. Absolute plans to integrate FirmGuard with its firmware-embedded Absolute Persistence technology, adding continuous firmware integrity monitoring.

Belgian application security firm Aikido Security acquired OutKept and Cyberly to launch Noon, a workforce security business. OutKept provides phishing simulations, while Cyberly develops AI-powered attack simulations and employee AI usage tracking tools. Anthropic agreed to acquire Opaque Systems, a confidential AI company that originated from UC Berkeley research. Anthropic described the deal as licensing Opaque's technology and hiring some of its engineers, including CEO Aaron Fulkerson and CTO Rishabh Poddar. Canadian AI developer Cohere signed a letter of intent to acquire AISLE, a startup focused on finding and patching vulnerabilities in critical software.

AISLE's approximately 50 employees will join Cohere, which is establishing a cybersecurity unit called Cohere Cyber. Hex-Rays, known for its IDA Pro reverse engineering tool, agreed to acquire HexAI, an Israeli startup founded in 2025. HexAI's AI agents analyse source code and binaries to uncover vulnerabilities, malware, and backdoors. Quantum computing company IonQ agreed to acquire zero trust security firm Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion. IonQ will combine its post-quantum cryptography with Elisity's IdentityGraph platform, which enforces least-privilege access for various entities.

Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint agreed to acquire data security company Varonis for roughly $6.3 billion in cash. The companies aim to offer a unified platform for discovering, protecting, and controlling access to sensitive data, along with preventing data loss. The articles do not say who is responsible for overseeing these deals or include statements from the companies beyond the deal descriptions.
